common_confusions: BC-MIS-06014 (average value and accumulated amount treated as the same quantity)
BC-MIS-06025 (an interpretation counted as complete once the quantity is named)
diagnostic_archetypes: BC-QA-06015 (interpreting a definite integral in context with units)
adaptive.mastered_if: The sentence written under a contextual rate graph names the accumulated quantity, its units, and the interval of accumulation together, so the area between the graph of f and the x axis over that interval is described as the change in the quantity whose rate is f, not as a value of f. The learner keeps the integral from a to b apart from the same integral divided by b minus a, and the wording survives both a graph of the rate and a displayed integral expression, with neither BC-ERR-06029 (interval or units dropped from the interpretation) nor BC-ERR-06030 (an average value expression called a total) appearing.
adaptive.partially_mastered_if: A correct quantity is named and the rest of the sentence thins out. BC-ERR-06029 shows as an interpretation that identifies what accumulates but leaves off the interval, or that attaches rate units where accumulated units belong. BC-ERR-06030 shows as a displayed average value expression read as the total over the interval. On BC-QA-06015 the value and the quantity are right while the interpretation point fails on the missing half of the required content.
adaptive.prerequisite_gap_if: Notation reading is the underlying break, BC-PRQ-06005, and the tell is that f(t) and f prime of t are used interchangeably in the sentence, or the integrand is described as an amount already present rather than a rate per unit input, so no interpretation can be assembled correctly even when the graph is read well.
adaptive.remediation_target: BC-MIS-06014 (separating the integral from the integral divided by the interval length) for the conceptual failure. Where the mathematics is right and only the sentence is short, the target is BC-MIS-06025 (the interval and the units belong in the statement).

skills.assessability_basis: no archetype requiring at most two skills names this skill; assessable only inside multi-skill parts
skills.description_formal: Given a graph of a rate function f in context, state that the area of the region between the graph and the x axis over an interval is the accumulated change in the quantity whose rate is f over that interval.
skills.description_plain: Say what the area between a rate graph and the axis measures in the situation described.
skills.name: Interpret the area under a rate of change graph as accumulated change

common_confusions: BC-MIS-06025 (an interpretation counted as complete once the quantity is named)
diagnostic_archetypes: BC-QA-06015 (interpreting a definite integral in context with units)
adaptive.mastered_if: Units are built as a product. Given a rate in units per unit input, the learner reports the unit of the accumulation as rate units times independent variable units, cancels the per correctly, and states the interval alongside, so gallons per second over seconds is reported as gallons and never as gallons per second. The same product holds whether the rate arrives as a table, as a graph, or as a displayed integral, and BC-ERR-06029 (units of the rate given in place of the accumulated units, or interval omitted) does not appear.
adaptive.partially_mastered_if: The accumulated quantity is named with the rate's own units still attached, which is BC-ERR-06029, or the units are right and the interval is missing. BC-QA-06015 scoring records exactly this split, and the BC-FRQ-2023-Q1-A and BC-FRQ-2026-Q1-B commentaries separate a correct sum whose interpretation lacks units or interval from an approximation failure, so the arithmetic can be intact while the unit statement is not.
adaptive.prerequisite_gap_if: When f(t) is read as an amount rather than as a rate at time t, the unit product has nothing to multiply, and that is BC-PRQ-06005 rather than a units gap. The tell is an interpretation that names a rate where a count was required, as the BC-FRQ-2026-Q1-B commentary describes.
adaptive.remediation_target: BC-MIS-06025 (what changes in the sentence when the interval changes) for the conceptual failure. A learner who knows the sentence must carry units but mishandles the multiplication of the two units points instead to BC-PRQ-06005 (what f(t) measures per unit input).

skills.assessability_basis: no archetype requiring at most two skills names this skill; assessable only inside multi-skill parts
skills.description_formal: Given the unit of a rate of change function and the unit of its independent variable, state the unit of the area of the region defined by the rate, which is the product of the two units.
skills.description_plain: Give the units of an accumulation as rate units times independent variable units.
skills.name: State the units of an accumulated change

common_confusions: BC-MIS-06012 (the definite integral read as unsigned area)
diagnostic_archetypes: BC-QA-06004 (definite integral evaluated from a graph by geometry)
adaptive.mastered_if: Sign is read off the rate without computing anything. A rate that is negative across an interval yields the statement that the quantity decreased, and a positive rate yields an increase, with the region below the axis carrying a negative contribution rather than a positive area. On BC-QA-06004 the learner attaches the minus sign to the pieces below the axis before adding, and describes the integral of a wholly negative rate as a negative number.
adaptive.partially_mastered_if: The direction is stated correctly in words while the computed integral still comes out positive, or the sign is handled on a graph with one crossing and lost when the rate dips below the axis twice. The BC-QA-06004 scoring note about linking a value to the correct label matters here, since a sign that is right for one interval may be carried to the other unchanged.
adaptive.prerequisite_gap_if: No prerequisite is recorded for this skill, so a failure that traces further back shows as an inability to say which quantity the graph is a rate for, at which point the question being answered is about reading the axes rather than about sign.
adaptive.remediation_target: BC-MIS-06012 (the integral of a rate that is negative on the whole interval) for the conceptual failure. When the sign rule is stated correctly and then dropped mid-computation, the target is instead BC-QA-06004 (attaching the negative sign to each piece before adding).

skills.assessability_basis: no archetype requiring at most two skills names this skill; assessable only inside multi-skill parts
skills.description_formal: Given the sign of a rate of change function on an interval, conclude that the accumulated change over that interval is positive when the rate is positive and negative when the rate is negative.
skills.description_plain: Decide whether the quantity rose or fell over an interval from whether the rate was positive or negative.
skills.name: Determine the sign of accumulated change from the sign of the rate

common_confusions: BC-MIS-06011 (area formulas recalled without their fractional factors)
diagnostic_archetypes: BC-QA-06004 (definite integral evaluated from a graph by geometry)
adaptive.mastered_if: Accumulated change over an interval comes out as a sum of signed areas, partitioned where the graph changes character, with one half b h for each triangle, one half times the sum of the parallel sides times the width for each trapezoid, and one half pi r squared for a semicircular piece. Regions below the axis enter negatively. The learner splits the interval at every axis crossing and labels each value with the integral it belongs to, so neither BC-ERR-06013 (a semicircle given the area of a full circle) nor BC-ERR-06014 (regions below the axis added as positive area) occurs.
adaptive.partially_mastered_if: Decomposition is right and a factor is missing. BC-ERR-06013 appears as pi r squared written for a semicircular or quarter-circular piece, and BC-ERR-06014 as every piece added positively so a signed integral is reported as a plain area. The BC-FRQ-2014-Q3-A commentary separates a failure to split at the crossing from a sign failure, and BC-FRQ-2024-Q4-A notes a positive value reported for an input left of the lower limit, where the reversal of limits was not applied. Values given without labels, as BC-FRQ-2022-Q3-A records, cost communication rather than method.
adaptive.prerequisite_gap_if: If the area of a single triangle or trapezoid read off the figure is wrong before any sign question arises, the break is BC-PRQ-06007 rather than this skill. The tell is that asking for one isolated region's area, with no integral attached, still produces the wrong number.
adaptive.remediation_target: BC-MIS-06011 (the halving factor in the triangle, trapezoid, and semicircle formulas) for the conceptual failure. When the formulas are sound and the signs are not, the target is BC-PRQ-06007 (areas from lengths read off the figure) for the measurement side and the signed-area step of BC-QA-06004 for the sign side.

skills.assessability_basis: no archetype requiring at most two skills names this skill; assessable only inside multi-skill parts
skills.description_formal: Given a rate of change function whose graph consists of line segments, compute the accumulated change over an interval as the sum of the signed areas of the resulting triangles, rectangles, and trapezoids.
skills.description_plain: Add up triangle and rectangle areas under a rate graph to get the total change.
skills.name: Compute accumulated change from a piecewise linear rate graph using geometry

common_confusions: BC-MIS-06002 (the endpoint convention treated as cosmetic)
diagnostic_archetypes: BC-QA-06001 (Riemann sum from a table with over or under estimate reasoning)
adaptive.mastered_if: The sample point is the centre of each subinterval, found as the average of the two partition points, and it is evaluated in f whether f arrives as a formula, as a graph to read, or as a table that already lists midpoint values. Each midpoint value is multiplied by its own subinterval width and the products are added, and the learner treats the midpoint choice as a different sample rule from left or right rather than as a label, so the value differs from the left and right sums on the same partition.
adaptive.partially_mastered_if: Endpoint sample values are used where midpoints were named, which BC-FRQ-2013-Q3-C and BC-FRQ-2026-Q1-B both record as a misread convention, and in 2026 a completely correct left or right sum still reaches the value point by sg-26:3. A second partial state is the sum computed correctly with the division by the interval length omitted, so an average is reported as a total.
adaptive.prerequisite_gap_if: Midpoints taken as the average of the endpoints but widths assumed common across an uneven partition is BC-PRQ-06012, and the tell is a correct midpoint list paired with one repeated width.
adaptive.remediation_target: BC-MIS-06002 (different sample points give different sums) for the conceptual failure. When the midpoint rule is held and the arithmetic of the widths is not, the target is BC-PRQ-06012 (nonuniform subinterval widths).

skills.assessability_basis: no archetype requiring at most two skills names this skill; assessable only inside multi-skill parts
skills.description_formal: Given a function represented graphically, numerically, or analytically and a partition, approximate the integral as the sum over subintervals of f at the midpoint of the subinterval multiplied by its width.
skills.description_plain: Use the value at the centre of each subinterval times its width and add.
skills.name: Compute a midpoint Riemann sum

diagnostic_archetypes: BC-QA-06001 (Riemann sum from a table with over or under estimate reasoning)
adaptive.mastered_if: No table is supplied and the learner builds one. The interval length divided by the number of equal subintervals gives the width, the partition points are listed, and the sample values are either evaluated from the formula or read off the graph at those inputs before any product is written. The assembled sum shows one product per subinterval under whichever rule was named, left, right, midpoint, or trapezoidal, and the factor count matches the subinterval count.
adaptive.partially_mastered_if: The width is found correctly and the sample inputs drift, so values are read at the wrong partition points, or the requested rule is replaced by a familiar one. BC-FRQ-2013-Q3-C records endpoint samples used where midpoints were named, BC-FRQ-2015-Q3-B and BC-FRQ-2022-Q4-C record left endpoints used where the stem named right, and BC-FRQ-2021-Q1-B records the integrand itself misread, with density values summed and the radius factor dropped, which leaves the sum rule intact.
adaptive.prerequisite_gap_if: Evaluating f at a stated input, or telling f from f prime and from f of g of x, is BC-PRQ-06005, and the tell is that the partition and the width are correct while the values placed against them are not the function's values at those inputs.
adaptive.remediation_target: BC-PRQ-06005 (function notation and evaluation at a stated input) for the conceptual failure, since the sample values must be produced rather than copied. Where the values are right and the assembly is not, the target is BC-QA-06001 (multiply each value by the width of its subinterval, then sum).

skills.assessability_basis: no archetype requiring at most two skills names this skill; assessable only inside multi-skill parts
skills.description_formal: Given a function presented graphically or analytically together with a number of equal subintervals, determine the subinterval width, obtain the required function values, and assemble the Riemann or trapezoidal sum.
skills.description_plain: Read or evaluate the needed function values yourself, then build the sum.
skills.name: Compute a Riemann sum for a function given by a graph or a formula

diagnostic_archetypes: BC-QA-06014 (converting between a limit of Riemann sums in sigma notation and a definite integral)
adaptive.mastered_if: Every term written out is a product, a value of f at a sample point times the width of its subinterval, and the index of summation is walked from its lower limit to its upper limit so the count of terms matches n. The expanded string keeps the width factor visible rather than folding it away, and BC-ERR-06003 (tabulated values added with no width factor) does not occur in the analytic setting of BC-REP-01.
adaptive.partially_mastered_if: Terms are produced in the right number but one factor is dropped, which is BC-ERR-06003, the response adding function values without multiplying each by a subinterval width, and the consequence is that neither the form nor the answer is credited because no product ever appears. A nearby partial state is an expansion whose general term is copied correctly but whose index range is off by one, so the first or last product is missing while the structure is sound.
adaptive.prerequisite_gap_if: BC-PRQ-06006 is the earlier failure that looks like this one, and the sign is that the lower and upper limits of the sigma expression are misread or the general term is evaluated at the index itself rather than at the sample point built from the index, so the expansion is wrong before any calculus idea is used.
adaptive.remediation_target: BC-PRQ-06006 (summation notation, its index, limits, and general term) for the conceptual failure of not reading the sigma expression as an instruction to list terms; a procedural failure that loses the width factor points instead to BC-ERR-06003 as the behaviour to observe.

skills.assessability_basis: no archetype requiring at most two skills names this skill; assessable only inside multi-skill parts
skills.description_formal: Given a Riemann sum written in sigma notation, expand it into the sum of products, each of which is a value of the function at a point in a subinterval multiplied by the length of that subinterval.
skills.description_plain: Write out the terms of a sigma expression as products of a value and a width.
skills.name: Expand summation notation into an explicit Riemann sum

diagnostic_archetypes: BC-QA-06014 (converting between a limit of Riemann sums in sigma notation and a definite integral)
adaptive.mastered_if: Given f, the endpoints a and b, and n equal pieces, the sigma expression is assembled with delta x written as (b minus a) over n and the sample point written in terms of the index, for instance a plus i times delta x for right endpoints, and the index limits are chosen to match that choice of sample point. The width factor multiplies the function value inside the sigma rather than sitting outside by accident, and the expression reproduces the intended partition when read back term by term.
adaptive.partially_mastered_if: The width is correct but the sample point expression is not anchored at a, so the sum describes a partition of the wrong interval. Another intermediate state comes from the tabulated analogues in BC-FRQ-2021-Q1-B and BC-FRQ-2022-Q4-C, where the named endpoint rule is not applied or a uniform width is imposed on a nonuniform partition, both of which show the sample point and width choices being made by habit rather than from the stated partition.
adaptive.prerequisite_gap_if: BC-PRQ-06006 is the underlying gap when the sigma expression has no coherent index, limits, and general term, and the tell is that the learner can describe the partition in words or in a picture but cannot place delta x and the sample point into a single indexed term.
adaptive.remediation_target: BC-PRQ-06006 (summation notation with an index, limits, and a general term) for the conceptual failure of not seeing the sum as a parametrised list; a procedural failure in forming (b minus a) over n and the sample point points instead to BC-QA-06014, whose first two steps separate the general term into a value and a width.

skills.assessability_basis: no archetype requiring at most two skills names this skill; assessable only inside multi-skill parts
skills.description_formal: Given f, an interval [a,b], and n equal subintervals, express the corresponding Riemann sum in sigma notation with subinterval width (b minus a) over n and the appropriate sample points.
skills.description_plain: Build the sigma expression from the function, the endpoints, and the number of subintervals.
skills.name: Write a Riemann sum in sigma notation for a given function, interval, and partition

diagnostic_archetypes: BC-QA-06014 (converting between a limit of Riemann sums in sigma notation and a definite integral)
adaptive.mastered_if: Reading a limit of Riemann sums, the response pulls the width factor out of the general term to recover delta x, deduces the interval length b minus a from it, reads the sample point expression to fix the lower limit a, and then writes the definite integral from a to b of the recovered integrand. The letter used for the index disappears and the variable of integration is introduced fresh, and the answer is an integral rather than a numerical value, since no antidifferentiation is asked for here.
adaptive.partially_mastered_if: The integrand is recovered but the limits of integration are guessed, typically 0 to 1 regardless of the sample point, which shows the second and third steps of BC-QA-06014 being skipped. A further intermediate state is an integral written with the index still present in the integrand, so the limit of the sum was rewritten symbol for symbol rather than interpreted.
adaptive.prerequisite_gap_if: BC-SKL-06012 is the earlier failure hiding here when the learner cannot expand the sigma expression into explicit products, so the value and width parts of the general term are never separated. BC-SKL-01006 shows up when the limit statement as n approaches infinity is treated as decoration and the response works with a fixed n, and BC-PRQ-06006 shows up when the index limits themselves cannot be read.
adaptive.remediation_target: BC-SKL-01006 (interpreting a limit statement given in analytic notation) when the conceptual role of the limiting process is absent; a procedural failure to split the general term into a value and a width points instead to BC-SKL-06012 (expanding summation notation into an explicit Riemann sum).

skills.assessability_basis: no archetype requiring at most two skills names this skill; assessable only inside multi-skill parts
skills.description_formal: Given a limit of Riemann sums as n approaches infinity or as the maximum subinterval width approaches 0, identify the integrand, the lower limit, and the upper limit, and write the equivalent definite integral.
skills.description_plain: Read the integrand and the limits of integration out of a limit of sums.
skills.name: Convert the limit of a Riemann sum into a definite integral

diagnostic_archetypes: BC-QA-06014 (converting between a limit of Riemann sums in sigma notation and a definite integral)
adaptive.mastered_if: Starting from a definite integral of a continuous function over [a,b], the learner produces the limit as n approaches infinity of a sigma expression whose width is (b minus a) over n and whose sample point is stated explicitly, for instance a plus i times that width, and the integrand is evaluated at that sample point rather than at the bare index. The direction of this construction is understood as the reverse of reading an integral out of a sum, and the interval endpoints appear in the sum only through the width and the sample point, never as limits of summation.
adaptive.partially_mastered_if: A sum of the right shape appears but the width is written as 1 over n with a and b forgotten, so the construction only works on an interval of length one. Another state is a sigma expression assembled correctly with the limit as n approaches infinity omitted, which leaves an approximation where an equality was required.
adaptive.prerequisite_gap_if: BC-SKL-06013 is the earlier skill that fails first, and the sign is that the learner can say what the answer should look like but cannot build the sigma expression for a stated function, interval, and partition. BC-PRQ-06006 is implicated when the index and its limits are themselves unstable.
adaptive.remediation_target: BC-PRQ-06006 (summation notation and the general term) when the conceptual link between an integral and an indexed sum is missing; a procedural failure to produce the width and sample point points instead to BC-SKL-06013 (writing a Riemann sum in sigma notation for a given function, interval, and partition).

skills.assessability_basis: no archetype requiring at most two skills names this skill; assessable only inside multi-skill parts
skills.description_formal: Given a definite integral of a continuous function over [a,b], write an equivalent limit of Riemann sums with an explicit subinterval width and sample point.
skills.description_plain: Go the other way and write the integral as a limit of sums.
skills.name: Express a definite integral as the limit of a Riemann sum

diagnostic_archetypes: BC-QA-06014 (converting between a limit of Riemann sums in sigma notation and a definite integral)
adaptive.mastered_if: The statement given includes the continuity hypothesis on [a,b], names n subintervals, names delta x sub i as the width of the ith subinterval, names x sub i star as a sample point in that subinterval, and says that the definite integral from a to b of f(x) dx equals the limit of the sums as the maximum subinterval width approaches 0 rather than merely as n grows. The learner can give the statement both in symbols (BC-REP-01) and in a sentence of ordinary words (BC-REP-04), and keeps the sample point arbitrary rather than fixed at an endpoint.
adaptive.partially_mastered_if: The limit is stated as n approaching infinity with no mention of the subinterval widths, which is correct only for equal partitions and shows the general definition has been collapsed into the uniform case. Another intermediate state names the pieces of notation correctly but omits the continuity hypothesis, so the statement is offered without the condition that makes it hold.
adaptive.prerequisite_gap_if: BC-PRQ-06006 is the gap masquerading as a definition failure, visible when delta x sub i and x sub i star are recited as sounds but the indexed general term cannot be assembled or read back. BC-TOP-0102 is implicated when the phrase about a limit approaching 0 carries no meaning for the learner.
adaptive.remediation_target: BC-TOP-0102 (the limit idea behind the definition) for the conceptual failure of treating the definition as a memorised string; a procedural failure to name the indexed pieces points instead to BC-PRQ-06006 (summation notation with an index, limits, and a general term).

skills.assessability_basis: no archetype requiring at most two skills names this skill; assessable only inside multi-skill parts
skills.description_formal: State that for f continuous on [a,b] the definite integral from a to b of f(x) dx is the limit of Riemann sums as the maximum subinterval width approaches 0, naming n, delta x sub i, and the sample point x sub i star.
skills.description_plain: Recite the definition, including that the subinterval widths go to zero.
skills.name: State the limit definition of the definite integral

common_confusions: BC-MIS-06024 (the variable of integration taken to be the independent variable)
diagnostic_archetypes: BC-QA-06012 (differentiating an accumulation function with a variable upper limit and evaluating the derivative at a point)
adaptive.mastered_if: The accumulation is set up as g(x) equal to the integral from a to x of f(t) dt, with the fixed starting input a in the lower limit, the independent variable x alone in the upper limit, and a bound variable of integration whose letter differs from x. Where a context supplies an initial amount, the setup reads as that initial amount plus the integral of the net rate, as the second point of BC-FRQ-2015-Q1-D requires, and the expression is a function of x rather than a number. BC-ERR-06028 (the answer left in terms of the dummy variable) does not appear, and the same setup is produced from a formula, from a graph, and from a verbal context (BC-REP-01, BC-REP-02, BC-REP-05).
adaptive.partially_mastered_if: The integral is written with the same letter in the upper limit and inside the integrand, the notation error the BC-FRQ-2015-Q1-D commentary records, which is the setup form of BC-ERR-06028. A separate intermediate state drops the initial amount and equates net change with the amount present, or integrates only the inflow when the context gives a net rate, so the structure of the accumulation is incomplete rather than the notation being wrong.
adaptive.prerequisite_gap_if: BC-PRQ-06013 is the earlier failure that looks like a setup failure, and the sign is that the learner sees no difference between the letter inside the integral and the letter in the upper limit. BC-PRQ-06005 is implicated when f(t) and f(x) are not read as the same function evaluated at different inputs, so the learner cannot say what object g is.
adaptive.remediation_target: BC-PRQ-06013 (bound variables and the dummy variable convention) for the conceptual failure about which letter lives inside the integral; a procedural failure that omits the initial amount or the net structure points instead to BC-FRQ-2015-Q1-D, whose second point is the equation joining the initial amount to the integral.

skills.assessability_basis: no archetype requiring at most two skills names this skill; assessable only inside multi-skill parts
skills.description_formal: Given a rate or a function f and a starting input a, represent the accumulation as g(x) = the integral from a to x of f(t) dt, using a bound variable of integration distinct from the independent variable.
skills.description_plain: Set up g(x) as the integral from a fixed start to x.
skills.name: Write an accumulation function as a definite integral with a variable upper limit

common_confusions: BC-MIS-06023 (the Fundamental Theorem of Calculus part one applied as a fixed template with no chain rule)
BC-MIS-06024 (the variable of integration taken to be the independent variable)
diagnostic_archetypes: BC-QA-06012 (differentiating an accumulation function with a variable upper limit and evaluating the derivative at a point)
adaptive.mastered_if: With f continuous on an interval containing a, the response states that g prime of x equals f of x and attributes it to the Fundamental Theorem of Calculus part one, then uses that identity rather than restating it, for instance reading increase of g from where f is positive as BC-FRQ-2021-Q4-A asks, or supplying g prime as one factor inside a product rule as BC-FRQ-2021-Q4-B asks. The derivative is expressed in the independent variable, so BC-ERR-06028 (an answer left in terms of the dummy variable) is absent, and the response does not report g prime as g itself. Both a formula for f (BC-REP-01) and a graph of f (BC-REP-02) support the same conclusion.
adaptive.partially_mastered_if: The theorem is quoted and the theorem point earned while the value is wrong, which is the pattern behind BC-ERR-06027 in its simple form and behind the BC-FRQ-2021-Q4-B distractor where the product rule is correct but the imported accumulation value is not. A second state is BC-ERR-06028, the integrand evaluated at t so the derivative never reaches the independent variable. A third is the BC-FRQ-2021-Q4-A behaviour of correct intervals with no reason attached, or intervals reported for f itself instead of for the accumulation.
adaptive.prerequisite_gap_if: BC-SKL-06017 is the earlier failure wearing this one's clothes, and the tell is that the function being differentiated was never written as an integral from a fixed lower limit to x, so there is nothing for the theorem to act on. BC-PRQ-06013 shows when the dummy variable and the upper limit are not held apart even before differentiation.
adaptive.remediation_target: BC-PRQ-06013 (bound variables and the dummy variable convention) for the conceptual failure that leaves the derivative in terms of t; a procedural failure to produce the value after the theorem is stated points instead to BC-SKL-06017 (writing the accumulation as an integral with a variable upper limit).

skills.assessability_basis: no archetype requiring at most two skills names this skill; assessable only inside multi-skill parts
skills.description_formal: Given g(x) = the integral from a to x of f(t) dt with f continuous on an interval containing a, conclude that g'(x) = f(x) for x in that interval.
skills.description_plain: Apply the Fundamental Theorem of Calculus part one to get g'(x) = f(x).
skills.name: Differentiate an accumulation function with a variable upper limit

common_confusions: BC-MIS-06011 (area formulas recalled without their fractional factors)
BC-MIS-06012 (the definite integral treated as unsigned area)
diagnostic_archetypes: BC-QA-06003 (an accumulation function analysed from a graph of the integrand made of segments and circular arcs)
adaptive.mastered_if: Signed area does the work. From the graph of f the learner splits the region at each crossing of the x axis, computes each piece with the right formula, one half base times height for a triangle and one half pi r squared for a semicircular piece, and subtracts the pieces lying below the axis before reporting g at the requested input, exactly the single value point of BC-FRQ-2014-Q3-A. Neither BC-ERR-06013 (a semicircular piece given pi r squared) nor BC-ERR-06014 (regions below the axis added as positive area) is present, and a negative value for g is accepted without hesitation when the graph calls for it.
adaptive.partially_mastered_if: The decomposition is correct and the arithmetic is not, in the two documented ways. BC-ERR-06013 gives the semicircle the full circle formula, losing the value point while leaving the method visible. BC-ERR-06014 adds every piece positively, so the reported number is total area rather than a signed integral, and the BC-FRQ-2021-Q4-D commentary notes the same error reaching a later part through an imported endpoint value. A third state omits the split at the crossing entirely, which the BC-FRQ-2014-Q3-A distractors record as a skipped decomposition step.
adaptive.prerequisite_gap_if: BC-SKL-06028 is the earlier skill that fails first, and the tell is that the learner can say g equals a signed area but cannot get a number out of a graph made of segments and arcs for any fixed pair of limits. BC-PRQ-06007 is implicated when lengths are read off the figure correctly but the area formula for a trapezoid or a circular piece cannot be produced.
adaptive.remediation_target: BC-SKL-06028 (evaluating a definite integral from a graph using area formulas) for the conceptual failure about signed area; a procedural failure in the formulas themselves, such as a dropped factor of one half, points instead to BC-PRQ-06007 (area formulas for rectangles, triangles, trapezoids, circles, and semicircles).

skills.assessability_basis: no archetype requiring at most two skills names this skill; assessable only inside multi-skill parts
skills.description_formal: Given the graph of f and g(x) = the integral from a to x of f(t) dt, evaluate g at a stated input by computing the signed area of the region between the graph of f and the x axis from a to that input.
skills.description_plain: Find g at a point by measuring signed area from the start value to that point.

diagnostic_archetypes: BC-QA-06012 (accumulation function with a variable, possibly composite, upper limit differentiated and then evaluated at a point)
adaptive.mastered_if: Before any differentiation happens, the response says that f must be continuous on an interval containing a and x, and only then writes that the derivative of the integral from a to x of f(t) dt equals f(x). The hypothesis survives the composite case in BC-QA-06012, where the upper limit is a function of x and the chain rule factor is attached to the upper limit while the continuity requirement is still stated about the integrand. No named errors are catalogued for this skill in the record, so the evidence rests on the hypothesis being volunteered rather than supplied by the question stem.
adaptive.partially_mastered_if: The conclusion is produced correctly and the hypothesis is omitted, or continuity is asserted about the accumulation function instead of about f. The BC-FRQ-2024-Q5-A scoring behaviour shows the neighbouring procedural slips that accompany this state, where the integrand is antidifferentiated instead of read off by the theorem, or a chain rule factor is introduced although the upper limit is plain x. In BC-FRQ-2025-Q4-A the theorem point can still be earned through an implied application, so a response that uses the theorem silently and never names continuity sits here.
adaptive.prerequisite_gap_if: The response cannot say what the derivative of an accumulation function is at all, which points back to BC-TOP-0115 rather than to the hypothesis itself. The tell is that the difficulty appears when asked to write the conclusion, not when asked what f must satisfy.
adaptive.remediation_target: BC-TOP-0115 (the statement of the Fundamental Theorem of Calculus part one, including which function carries the continuity requirement); a procedural failure to evaluate the resulting derivative points instead to BC-QA-06012 (substituting the requested input into the integrand)

common_confusions: BC-MIS-06007 (the plotted curve is taken to be the function under discussion, so features of g are read off the integrand)
diagnostic_archetypes: BC-QA-06003 (accumulation function analysed from a graph of the integrand made of segments and circular arcs)
adaptive.mastered_if: Intervals of increase for g are given as the intervals where the plotted f lies above the axis, and intervals of decrease where f lies below, with the reason phrased about the graph of f rather than about g. The Fundamental Theorem step is visible, so g prime is written equal to f before any sign reading, and the answer is confined to the stated domain. The confusion recorded as BC-ERR-06008, reading features of g straight off the visible features of the plotted curve, is absent, and positivity of f is kept separate from f rising.
adaptive.partially_mastered_if: Correct intervals arrive with a reason phrased about g itself, which BC-FRQ-2014-Q3-B and BC-FRQ-2018-Q3-C both record as a referent failure that costs the reason point while the answer point stands. Another intermediate state gives only the intervals of increase when both halves were asked for, or extends the intervals past the stated subinterval, which BC-FRQ-2024-Q4-B lists as a domain slip. Partial forms of BC-ERR-06008, where the zeros of g are reported instead of the intervals of increase, show the function and its derivative being exchanged in one part while other parts stay correct.
adaptive.prerequisite_gap_if: BC-SKL-06018 is missing when the response never writes g prime equal to f, so the sign reading is applied to whichever curve is in front of it. The tell-tale sign is that the sign analysis itself is competent while the object it is applied to is wrong.
adaptive.remediation_target: BC-MIS-06007 (separating the plotted integrand from the accumulation function defined by it) for the conceptual failure; when the referent is right and only the written reason is loose, the target is BC-ERR-06008 (tying the stated reason to the given graph of f)

common_confusions: BC-MIS-06006 (concavity and monotonicity treated as the same property, so the two justifications are exchanged)
BC-MIS-06009 (restating a definition believed to count as a reason)
diagnostic_archetypes: BC-QA-06003 (accumulation function analysed from a graph of the integrand made of segments and circular arcs)
adaptive.mastered_if: Concave up intervals for g are matched to the intervals where the plotted f is increasing and concave down to where f is decreasing, with the justification naming that rise or fall of f. A decreasing but concave up stretch of f is handled without trouble, so rising is kept apart from being positive. The stated reason ties the claim to the given graph, which is what BC-ERR-06010 lacks, and the object of the claim stays the accumulation function rather than the plotted curve, which is what BC-ERR-06008 loses.
adaptive.partially_mastered_if: Intervals where the plotted function is positive are reported as the concave up intervals, which BC-FRQ-2021-Q4-A and BC-FRQ-2014-Q3-B both describe as positivity and increase conflated. Correct intervals with no reason at all also sit here, since BC-FRQ-2021-Q4-A awards its single point for intervals together with a reason. A third state supplies the right intervals but phrases the reason about the accumulation function only, the referent failure BC-ERR-06010 describes.
adaptive.prerequisite_gap_if: A missing BC-SKL-06018 leaves the response with no statement that g prime equals f, so the monotonicity of f is never connected to the concavity of g and the analysis is carried out on the visible curve. The tell is that the monotonic stretches of f are identified correctly and the conclusion is labelled with the wrong function.
adaptive.remediation_target: BC-MIS-06006 (separating whether a curve rises from whether it bends upward) for the conceptual failure; a justification that names the right feature but not the given representation points instead to BC-ERR-06010 (anchoring the reason to the plotted graph of f)

common_confusions: BC-MIS-06007 (the plotted curve is taken to be the function under discussion)
BC-MIS-06009 (restating a definition believed to count as a reason)
diagnostic_archetypes: BC-QA-06003 (accumulation function analysed from a graph of the integrand made of segments and circular arcs)
adaptive.mastered_if: A single description of g holds all four pieces at once, the value at the starting input where the integral from a to a is zero, the intervals of rise and fall from the sign of f, the extrema at the sign changes of f, and the concavity from whether f is rising or falling. The description or sketch is consistent with itself, so a stated maximum sits at the end of a stated interval of increase, and each claim is attributed to a feature of the plotted f rather than to g, which is what BC-ERR-06010 omits. The curve being described is never the curve on the page, so BC-ERR-06008 is absent.
adaptive.partially_mastered_if: Some features are read from the right function and others from the plotted curve, which produces a description that contradicts itself, the mixed form of BC-ERR-06008. Another state gives an internally consistent description with every reason phrased about g changing concavity or g turning, which is BC-ERR-06010 and costs the reason points while the answer points stand. BC-FRQ-2025-Q4-A also records the accumulated area to the input reported in place of the derivative statement, so the function and its derivative are exchanged in the opening step and the rest of the description inherits it.
adaptive.prerequisite_gap_if: A description that is right about monotonicity and silent or wrong about bending points at BC-SKL-06025, while wrong inflection inputs with correct increase intervals point at BC-SKL-06024, and a wholesale failure of the sign reading points at BC-SKL-06022. The tell is that the assembly is orderly and exactly one of the three component claims is unsupported.
adaptive.remediation_target: BC-MIS-06007 (holding the plotted integrand and the accumulation function apart across a whole multi part description) for the conceptual failure; when each feature is located correctly and only the written support is generic, the target is BC-ERR-06010 (tying every claim about g to the given graph of f)

diagnostic_archetypes: BC-QA-06013 (supplied definite integral values combined through constant multiple, sum, reversal and adjacent interval properties)
adaptive.mastered_if: Given values for the integral of f and the integral of g over the same interval, a constant is pulled outside the integral sign and an integral of a sum or difference is split into the two supplied integrals before any number is substituted. The rewriting step is written out, so the requested integral is first matched to the supplied ones in the BC-QA-06013 manner and only then evaluated and simplified. The supplied values are used rather than ignored in favour of symbolic integration of an unspecified function, which BC-FRQ-2023-Q5-A and BC-FRQ-2023-Q5-C both record as a way of discarding the given data. No errors or misconceptions are catalogued for this skill in the record.
adaptive.partially_mastered_if: Linearity is applied to a sum and the constant multiple is left inside, or the constant is pulled out of a difference and distributed over only the first term. Another state reverses the order of subtraction, which BC-FRQ-2023-Q5-A lists as forcing a positive answer without identifying which function comes first. The BC-QA-06013 scoring behaviour notes that a correct value alone earns the point, so a rewriting that is right in structure and wrong in one substituted value sits in this band.
adaptive.prerequisite_gap_if: No prerequisite skills are recorded for this skill, and the earliest failure visible in the record is at BC-TOP level, showing as an inability to say what a definite integral over a stated interval denotes before any property is applied. The tell is that the properties are recited accurately and cannot be attached to the supplied numbers.
adaptive.remediation_target: BC-QA-06013 (matching a requested integral to the supplied ones before substituting) for the conceptual failure; an arithmetic or sign slip after a correct rewriting points instead to BC-SKL-06030 (the reversal of limits property, where the sign is decided)

diagnostic_archetypes: BC-QA-06013 (supplied definite integral values combined through constant multiple, sum, reversal and adjacent interval properties)
adaptive.mastered_if: Once the integral of f from a to b is known, the integral from b to a is reported as the negative of that value without recomputing anything, and the negation is attributed to the swapped limits rather than to the sign of f. In the BC-FRQ-2024-Q4-A setting the property is used for an input lying to the left of the fixed lower limit, with the supplied region area giving the magnitude and the reversal giving the sign. Values are labelled with the inputs they belong to, which BC-FRQ-2025-Q4-C requires before either value counts.
adaptive.partially_mastered_if: A positive value is reported for the input left of the lower limit, which BC-FRQ-2024-Q4-A records as the reversal property simply not applied. A second state applies the reversal and then also negates for a region below the axis that was already accounted for, so two sign decisions collide. BC-FRQ-2022-Q3-A describes the direction of accumulation from the known input reversed, and BC-FRQ-2025-Q4-C describes correct values attached to the wrong labels, both of which leave the property itself intact while the answer fails.
adaptive.prerequisite_gap_if: No prerequisite skills are listed here, and the failure that imitates this one comes from the magnitude rather than the sign, showing as a supplied region area ignored and the region estimated instead, which BC-FRQ-2024-Q4-A names directly. The tell is a correctly negated answer built on a wrong number.
adaptive.remediation_target: BC-QA-06013 (the reversal of limits as a statement about orientation of the interval) for the conceptual failure; a sign that is right with a magnitude that is not points instead to BC-SKL-06028 (evaluating the integral from the graph using area formulas)

diagnostic_archetypes: BC-QA-06013 (supplied integral values recombined using constant multiple, sum, reversal, and adjacent interval properties)
adaptive.mastered_if: Given the integral of f over [a,b] and over [b,c], the learner writes the integral from a to c as the sum of the two supplied values, and when the missing piece is the middle one recovers it by subtracting rather than by re-integrating. The same additivity is used on a graph, where a region is cut at a crossing and the two signed pieces are added, and on a list of supplied numerical values under BC-QA-06013, where reversal of limits is combined with additivity in one rewrite. Regions below the axis enter with a negative sign, and the splitting point is chosen at the crossing rather than at a convenient tick mark.
adaptive.partially_mastered_if: Additivity is applied correctly on supplied numbers but breaks on a figure, where areas are added without signs so a region below the axis is counted as positive, or the interval is never split at the crossing at all so a single unsigned area is reported. Another intermediate state is the value being correct while the adjacent interval property is never stated in writing, which the 2019 Q3 part A rubric treats as a skipped communication step even though the arithmetic holds. A correct decomposition whose value is then carried wrongly into a later part is an import error, not a failure of additivity.
adaptive.prerequisite_gap_if: No prerequisite skill is listed for this one, so a wrong value here traces back to reading the figure rather than to an earlier skill. The tell is a correct sum structure with wrong individual pieces, such as a quarter circle given the area of a full circle, which shows the geometric area formulas rather than the interval property are the failure.
adaptive.remediation_target: BC-QA-06013 (rewriting a requested integral in terms of the supplied ones) for the conceptual failure; when the structure is right and only the signed pieces are wrong, the procedural target is BC-SKL-06070 (reading signed area off the figure)

diagnostic_archetypes: BC-QA-06013 (supplied integral values recombined using constant multiple, sum, reversal, and adjacent interval properties)
adaptive.mastered_if: The learner writes the integral of f from a to a equal to 0 without computing anything, and uses that fact to fix the starting value of an accumulation function, so g(a) is reported as 0 whatever f looks like near a. Within BC-QA-06013, a degenerate piece appearing after additivity or reversal is dropped immediately rather than estimated from the figure.
adaptive.partially_mastered_if: The zero is stated in isolation but not carried into an accumulation function, so a starting value is computed from the shape of f near a instead of being read off as 0. A second intermediate state is treating the degenerate integral as undefined rather than zero, which leaves the rewrite under BC-QA-06013 unfinished.
adaptive.prerequisite_gap_if: Nothing earlier is listed as required here. When the answer is wrong, the tell is that the learner never identified which limit was which, so the degeneracy was not noticed rather than not known.
adaptive.remediation_target: BC-QA-06013 (matching each requested integral to the supplied ones before evaluating) for the conceptual failure, with no separate procedural target since the evaluation is a single stated fact

common_confusions: BC-MIS-06026 (the Fundamental Theorem of Calculus part two treated as needing no hypotheses)
diagnostic_archetypes: BC-QA-06013 (supplied integral values recombined using constant multiple, sum, reversal, and adjacent interval properties)
adaptive.mastered_if: A jump or removable discontinuity inside the interval is spotted in the given definition, the integral is split there, each continuous piece is antidifferentiated with its own expression, and the pieces are added. The learner says that the value at the single point does not affect the integral, and states that the Fundamental Theorem part two is being applied piecewise because its continuity hypothesis holds on each piece and not across the whole interval. Both a piecewise formula and a graph of such a function are handled the same way.
adaptive.partially_mastered_if: The discontinuity is noticed but the antiderivative of one branch is applied across the jump anyway, which is BC-ERR-06031 (the split at a discontinuity omitted, so a single expression is antidifferentiated across the jump) and costs the value point because that antiderivative is not valid on the whole interval. A weaker state is splitting correctly while asserting that the theorem applies directly to the original integrand, so the piecewise argument is performed without being justified.
adaptive.prerequisite_gap_if: When the split is made but the two pieces are then combined wrongly, the gap is BC-SKL-06031 (the adjacent interval property), and the tell is pieces that are individually right and a total that is neither their sum nor their difference.
adaptive.remediation_target: BC-MIS-06026 (the continuity hypothesis of the Fundamental Theorem part two) for the conceptual failure; procedural failure points instead to BC-SKL-06031 (adding the integrals of the continuous pieces)

diagnostic_archetypes: BC-QA-06008 (antiderivative or definite integral by substitution, with limits either converted or restored)
adaptive.mastered_if: An antiderivative F is produced for a continuous f, the integral from a to b is written as F(b) minus F(a) with that difference shown, and the constant of integration is dropped knowingly because it cancels. When the integrand is a composite times a constant multiple of the derivative of its inner expression, as in BC-QA-06008, the learner either back-substitutes before using the original limits or converts the limits to u, and never applies x limits to an expression still written in u. Endpoint values read off a figure are matched to the correct function, and the antiderivative of a derivative is written as the function itself rather than as its square.
adaptive.partially_mastered_if: The setup is right and the numerical value is wrong because the calculator was left in degree mode for a trigonometric integrand, which is BC-ERR-06032 (degree mode used where radian mode is required) and forfeits only the value point while leaving later points available. Other intermediate states are an indefinite integral left unevaluated so the definite integral requirement is not met, bounds imported from the wrong figure, and logarithm arithmetic failing at the limits while the antidifferentiation itself is correct.
adaptive.prerequisite_gap_if: If the endpoint subtraction is executed correctly on whatever expression was produced but the expression is wrong, the gap is BC-SKL-06040 (antidifferentiating power functions) or BC-PRQ-06002 (exponent rules for negative and fractional exponents), and the tell is a radical or reciprocal that was never rewritten as a power before the reverse power rule was attempted.
adaptive.remediation_target: BC-PRQ-06002 (exponent rules underneath any antiderivative of a power) for the conceptual failure; procedural failure points instead to BC-SKL-06040 (producing the antiderivative itself before any endpoint substitution)

common_confusions: BC-MIS-06026 (the Fundamental Theorem of Calculus part two treated as needing no hypotheses)
diagnostic_archetypes: BC-QA-06013 (supplied integral values recombined using constant multiple, sum, reversal, and adjacent interval properties)
adaptive.mastered_if: Both hypotheses are named before the conclusion is used, so the learner says that f is continuous on [a,b] and that F is an antiderivative of f on [a,b], and only then writes the integral from a to b of f(x) dx equal to F(b) minus F(a). Asked whether the theorem applies to an integrand with a jump inside the interval, the answer is no, with the continuity hypothesis given as the reason. In the verbal form of BC-QA-06013 the learner distinguishes the theorem from the properties that merely recombine supplied values.
adaptive.partially_mastered_if: The conclusion is quoted accurately while the hypotheses are left out, so F(b) minus F(a) is applied to any integrand offered. A related state is naming continuity but not the antiderivative condition, which shows up as the antiderivative of a derivative being written as a square of the function, the theorem being confused with a power rule. Reading the wrong curve off a figure, such as integrating the plotted function where its derivative was the integrand, is a graph-reading failure rather than a failure to hold the statement.
adaptive.prerequisite_gap_if: No earlier skill is listed for stating the theorem. When the statement is right and the use is wrong, the earlier failure is reading the figure, and the tell is endpoint values misread from the graph while the form F(b) minus F(a) is written correctly.
adaptive.remediation_target: BC-MIS-06026 (the hypotheses that license F(b) minus F(a)) for the conceptual failure; when the statement is sound and only its application slips, the target is BC-SKL-06034 (carrying out the endpoint substitution)

common_confusions: BC-MIS-06013 (the integral of a rate read as the amount of the quantity)
diagnostic_archetypes: BC-QA-06005 (net change from a rate with an initial condition supplied at one endpoint)
adaptive.mastered_if: Net change is written as a definite integral of the given rate over the stated interval, with limits in the variable the rate actually uses, so elapsed hours are substituted where the question supplies clock times. The learner separates the rate value at an endpoint from the accumulated amount and says which one the question asked for, and when two rates act on the quantity integrates only the one named. Units accompany the reported amount, and the numerical evaluation is done in radian mode for a trigonometric integrand.
adaptive.partially_mastered_if: The integral is written correctly and the number is wrong, a calculator workflow failure rather than an accumulation failure, including BC-ERR-06032 (degree mode left on for a trigonometric integrand), which forfeits the value point but not the later ones. Rounding short of the required accuracy sits in the same band. A different intermediate state is BC-ERR-06015 (the initial condition omitted, so the integral of the rate is reported as the quantity at the later input), which is the boundary between this skill and the one that builds on it.
adaptive.prerequisite_gap_if: When the wrong object is integrated, for instance f itself where f prime was the rate, the gap is BC-PRQ-06005 (reading function notation, composition, and evaluation), and the tell is a learner who cannot say which of the supplied symbols is the rate. If the integral is set up right and evaluated wrong by hand, the gap is BC-SKL-06034 (endpoint substitution).
adaptive.remediation_target: BC-MIS-06013 (accumulated change as distinct from the amount present) for the conceptual failure; procedural failure points instead to BC-SKL-06034 (evaluating the definite integral itself)

diagnostic_archetypes: BC-QA-06006 (rate in minus rate out accumulation, possibly combined with an initial amount)
adaptive.mastered_if: Inflow and outflow are identified by which one raises and which one lowers the quantity, and the net accumulation is written as one definite integral of inflow minus outflow over the shared interval rather than as two separate integrals bolted together afterwards. A constant outflow rate is handled as a constant inside the same integrand instead of being integrated as though it varied. When a variable upper limit is needed, the variable of integration is given a different letter from the limit, the notation point the rubric tracks in 2015 Q1 part D.
adaptive.partially_mastered_if: Only the inflow is integrated and the outflow never reaches the integrand, so the net rate structure is dropped while the accumulation machinery is otherwise intact. A second state is a correct integral of the difference presented as the amount present, with the initial amount left out, which the same rubric separates from the integral point. Using one letter for both the upper limit and the variable of integration is a notation slip that the rubric penalises even where the structure is right.
adaptive.prerequisite_gap_if: When the difference of rates is formed correctly but the accumulated amount is still wrong, the gap is BC-SKL-06036 (computing net change from a rate over an interval), and the tell is a correct net rate paired with limits that do not match the interval described.
adaptive.remediation_target: BC-QA-06006 (net rate as inflow minus outflow inside one integral) for the conceptual failure; procedural failure points instead to BC-SKL-06036 (integrating that net rate over the interval)

diagnostic_archetypes: BC-QA-06016 (selecting an antidifferentiation technique from the structure of the integrand)
adaptive.mastered_if: Radicals and reciprocals are rewritten as powers first, then the exponent is raised by one and the result divided by that new exponent, with the constant of integration attached whenever the answer is an indefinite integral. The exponent negative one is excluded by name rather than by accident. Term by term antidifferentiation of a polynomial is carried out completely, and under BC-QA-06016 the learner inspects the integrand's structural markers and rules out techniques whose preconditions fail before applying the reverse power rule.
adaptive.partially_mastered_if: The exponent is raised and the divisor is left off, so the antiderivative of a power is half remembered while the rest of the method is sound. A related state is the general solution being produced where a particular one was asked, the constant omitted after separating variables, as recorded in 2019 Q4 part C. Correct antiderivatives followed by wrong arithmetic at the limits, and copy errors carried in from an earlier part, are evaluation and transcription failures rather than antidifferentiation failures.
adaptive.prerequisite_gap_if: An integrand left in radical or reciprocal form, with the reverse power rule attempted on it directly, points to BC-PRQ-06002 (exponent rules including negative and fractional exponents). If the power rule itself cannot be reconstructed, the earlier skill is BC-SKL-02027 (deriving a power rule case from the limit definition), and the tell is a learner who treats the rule as a remembered string with no source.
adaptive.remediation_target: BC-PRQ-06002 (exponent rules that make a radical or reciprocal into a power) for the conceptual failure; procedural failure points instead to BC-SKL-02027 (the power rule case the reverse rule inverts)
