diagnostic_archetypes: BC-QA-06016 (several integrands of different structure are classified and the technique each structure calls for is named or applied)
adaptive.mastered_if: The integrand one over x is antidifferentiated as the natural logarithm of the absolute value of x, e to the x returns itself, and a constant base b to the x carries the reciprocal of ln b as its factor. An inner linear argument brings its own reciprocal constant down, and an improper upper bound is written with limit notation on the integral or on the exponential antiderivative rather than with infinity substituted into the expression, which is one of the three accepted forms in BC-FRQ-2026-Q5-D.
adaptive.partially_mastered_if: The exponential and reciprocal forms are named correctly but the reciprocal constant from the inner linear argument is dropped, so the antiderivative is a nonzero constant multiple of the correct one, the pattern BC-FRQ-2026-Q5-D records as the chain factor lost. Another intermediate state writes limit notation only on the final line instead of from the step where the improper bound first appears, and a third leaves the integral indefinite where the stem asked for a value.
adaptive.prerequisite_gap_if: Logarithm arithmetic collapses at the limits while the antiderivative itself is right, which points at BC-PRQ-06003 rather than this skill. The tell is a correct ln of an absolute value followed by a wrong difference of logarithms, or absolute value dropped from the logarithm of a linear expression.
adaptive.remediation_target: BC-PRQ-06003 (logarithm properties and the absolute value inside ln) for the conceptual failure; the procedural failure, where the form is named but the reciprocal constant or the limit notation is lost, stays inside BC-SKL-06041.

skills.assessability_basis: no archetype requiring at most two skills names this skill; assessable only inside multi-skill parts
skills.description_formal: Given an integrand of the form e to the x, a constant base raised to x, or one over x, determine the corresponding antiderivative, using the natural logarithm of the absolute value for the reciprocal form.
skills.description_plain: Recognise the forms whose antiderivatives are exponentials and natural logarithms.
skills.name: Antidifferentiate exponential and reciprocal integrands

diagnostic_archetypes: BC-QA-06016 (integrands of different structure are classified and the technique each one's markers select is named or applied)
adaptive.mastered_if: Each basic trigonometric integrand is matched to the differentiation rule it inverts, with the sign handled correctly so that the antiderivative of sine carries the minus and the antiderivative of cosine does not. Where the argument is a linear expression, the reciprocal of the inner coefficient appears in front, and where a product is recognisable as a trigonometric derivative it is read backwards directly rather than expanded. The constant of integration is present on every indefinite result.
adaptive.partially_mastered_if: Rules are inverted correctly in isolation but the inner constant is dropped from the sine antiderivative, which BC-FRQ-2024-Q5-D lists as the chain factor lost. A second state omits the constant of integration, treating an indefinite integral as definite, also recorded in that part. A third produces the right family with the sign reversed between sine and cosine.
adaptive.prerequisite_gap_if: The integrand needs a Pythagorean, double angle, or reciprocal identity before any antiderivative rule applies and the rewriting never happens, which is BC-PRQ-06004 failing and not this skill. A second earlier failure is BC-SKL-02035, where a limit that is a trigonometric derivative in disguise is not recognised as such, leaving no derivative rule to invert.
adaptive.remediation_target: BC-PRQ-06004 (identities that rewrite an integrand into a form with a basic antiderivative) for the conceptual failure; procedural loss of the inner constant or the constant of integration points instead to BC-SKL-06042 itself.

skills.assessability_basis: no archetype requiring at most two skills names this skill; assessable only inside multi-skill parts
skills.description_formal: Given an integrand that is a basic trigonometric function or a product recognisable as a trigonometric derivative, determine the antiderivative from the corresponding differentiation rule.
skills.description_plain: Read the trigonometric derivative rules backwards.
skills.name: Antidifferentiate basic trigonometric integrands

diagnostic_archetypes: BC-QA-06016 (a mixed set of integrands where each structure has to select its own technique)
adaptive.mastered_if: One over one plus x squared is read as arctangent and one over the square root of one minus x squared as arcsine, and the two are told apart by the structural marker rather than by guessing. A constant in place of the one is factored out so the form matches before the rule is applied, and a linear inner argument brings its reciprocal constant with it. The candidate can be differentiated back to the integrand as a check.
adaptive.partially_mastered_if: The inverse trigonometric family is identified but the wrong member is chosen, so a square root denominator is answered with arctangent or the reverse. In other work the form is matched only when the constants are already one, and any rescaling of the denominator sends the response toward an unrelated technique, which BC-QA-06016 exposes when the preconditions of the ruled-out techniques are never checked.
adaptive.prerequisite_gap_if: The derivatives of inverse sine, cosine, and tangent cannot be stated on demand, so there is nothing to invert. That is BC-SKL-03021 rather than this skill, and the tell is a correct structural reading of the integrand followed by a fabricated antiderivative.
adaptive.remediation_target: BC-SKL-03021 (stating the inverse trigonometric derivatives) for the conceptual failure; when the rule is known but the constants are not factored to match the form, the target is BC-PRQ-06004 (rewriting an integrand into a recognisable form).

skills.assessability_basis: no archetype requiring at most two skills names this skill; assessable only inside multi-skill parts
skills.description_formal: Given an integrand matching the derivative of an inverse trigonometric function, determine the antiderivative as that inverse trigonometric function.
skills.description_plain: Recognise the one over one plus x squared and one over the root of one minus x squared forms.
skills.name: Antidifferentiate integrands whose antiderivatives are inverse trigonometric

common_confusions: BC-MIS-06018 (an antiderivative is treated as a single function, so the arbitrary constant is decoration rather than part of the answer)
diagnostic_archetypes: BC-QA-06016 (integrands of differing structure, each classified and matched to the technique its markers select)
adaptive.mastered_if: Plus C appears on every indefinite result, and when a value of the antiderivative at a point is supplied it is substituted to solve for that constant, giving a single particular function rather than a family. The constant is attached at the antidifferentiation step, not after a later exponentiation, and the learner can name two functions differing by a constant that share the same derivative.
adaptive.partially_mastered_if: Antidifferentiation is correct and BC-ERR-06021 appears, the arbitrary constant omitted from an indefinite integral, which BC-FRQ-2024-Q5-D records as an indefinite integral treated as definite. In other work C is written but never solved for although an initial value was given, and in BC-FRQ-2015-Q5-D the decomposition is right while the logarithms arrive without absolute values or constant, a notation loss rather than a technique loss.
adaptive.prerequisite_gap_if: The antiderivative the constant would attach to is itself wrong on power functions with negative or fractional exponents, so BC-SKL-06040 is the earlier failure. The tell is a correctly placed plus C sitting on an incorrect power rule result.
adaptive.remediation_target: BC-MIS-06018 (the antiderivative as a family, not one function) for the conceptual failure; the procedural failure, where C is known to belong but is dropped under time pressure, points to BC-ERR-06021 (constant of integration omitted).

skills.assessability_basis: no archetype requiring at most two skills names this skill; assessable only inside multi-skill parts
skills.description_formal: Given an indefinite integral, include an arbitrary constant C in the answer, and when a value of the antiderivative at a point is supplied, solve for the particular value of C.
skills.description_plain: Write plus C, then solve for it when a value of the antiderivative is given.
skills.name: Include the constant of integration and determine it from an initial condition

common_confusions: BC-MIS-06018 (the antiderivative treated as unique, so a candidate differing by a constant is judged wrong)
diagnostic_archetypes: BC-QA-06016 (structural inspection of integrands, where verifying the result of the chosen technique closes the loop)
adaptive.mastered_if: Differentiating the candidate F returns the integrand f exactly, and the comparison is made term by term so that a missing reciprocal constant from a chain factor shows up as a mismatch. A candidate differing from a correct antiderivative only by an added constant is accepted rather than rejected, since the derivative of that constant is zero, and a candidate whose derivative differs by a nonzero multiple is rejected and named as such.
adaptive.partially_mastered_if: The differentiation is carried out but the verdict is wrong at the boundary case, so F plus three is called not an antiderivative because it does not match a remembered answer. Elsewhere the check is run only on the outer layer and a dropped inner constant survives it, leaving a constant multiple of the integrand accepted as the integrand.
adaptive.prerequisite_gap_if: No prerequisite is listed for this skill in the record, so a failure here traces to the differentiation itself rather than to a named earlier skill. The tell is a correct statement of what the check should produce followed by a derivative computed incorrectly.
adaptive.remediation_target: BC-MIS-06018 (many functions share one derivative) for the conceptual failure; when the criterion is understood but the derivative is mis-executed, the target is BC-SKL-06045 itself.

skills.assessability_basis: no archetype requiring at most two skills names this skill; assessable only inside multi-skill parts
skills.description_formal: Given a candidate antiderivative F and an integrand f, differentiate F and compare the result with f to confirm or reject that F is an antiderivative of f.
skills.description_plain: Differentiate the candidate and check it returns the integrand.
skills.name: Verify a proposed antiderivative by differentiating it

diagnostic_archetypes: BC-QA-06016 (integrands inspected for structural markers, with techniques whose preconditions fail ruled out)
adaptive.mastered_if: An integrand such as e to the negative t squared is identified as having no closed-form antiderivative, and the accumulation is then left as a definite integral or sent to numerical evaluation rather than forced through an antidifferentiation rule. When a tabulated or given initial value is present, the reported quantity is that value plus the definite integral of the rate over the stated interval, with the interval taken from the prompt and not extended back to time zero.
adaptive.partially_mastered_if: The integral form is set up but the initial condition is dropped and the integral alone is reported, one of the distinguishing failures in BC-FRQ-2024-Q1-C. Elsewhere the integrand is not recognised as needing technology and antidifferentiation is attempted by hand, and in BC-FRQ-2026-Q1-C the integral starts at day zero although the prompt fixed the interval, or the unrounded decimal is reported against a rounding instruction.
adaptive.prerequisite_gap_if: No prerequisite is listed for this skill in the record. When the failure is reading the initial value from the wrong row of the table, as BC-FRQ-2024-Q1-C describes, the breakdown is in table reading rather than in recognising the integrand.
adaptive.remediation_target: BC-SKL-06046 (accumulation represented by an integral when no elementary antiderivative exists) for the conceptual failure; the procedural failure, where the integral is right but the initial value or the interval is mishandled, points to BC-FRQ-2024-Q1-C scoring behaviour on the initial condition point.

skills.assessability_basis: no archetype requiring at most two skills names this skill; assessable only inside multi-skill parts
skills.description_formal: Given an integrand such as e to the negative t squared, recognise that it has no closed-form antiderivative and that the accumulation must be represented by a definite integral or approximated numerically.
skills.description_plain: Notice when no elementary antiderivative exists and keep the integral form.
skills.name: Recognise an integrand with no closed-form antiderivative

common_confusions: BC-MIS-06017 (a composite integrand is taken to guarantee that substitution applies, without checking that the inner derivative is present)
diagnostic_archetypes: BC-QA-06008 (a composite times a constant multiple of its inner derivative, taken through u, du, rewriting, antidifferentiating, and back-substitution or converted limits)
BC-QA-06016 (mixed integrands where the structure has to select the technique)
adaptive.mastered_if: u is stated explicitly as the inner expression, and the response can point to a constant multiple of the derivative of that inner expression sitting inside the integrand before committing to the technique. Where the integrand needs rewriting first, a constant is factored out or a fraction split so the du factor is exposed. Neither BC-ERR-06020, substitution attempted when the inner derivative is absent, nor BC-ERR-06019, the constant factor from the differential dropped, appears in the work.
adaptive.partially_mastered_if: A composite is spotted and substitution is launched on that alone, BC-ERR-06020, so the setup point for the technique is not earned and the line of work leads nowhere. In other attempts the choice of u is right and BC-ERR-06019 follows, the reciprocal constant from du never appearing, which BC-FRQ-2014-Q5-A records as a difference of boundary functions correct with the substitution constant dropped, and BC-FRQ-2024-Q3-C as the inner constant lost from a sine antiderivative.
adaptive.prerequisite_gap_if: The inner function and its derivative are present but hidden until the expression is rewritten, and no rewriting is attempted, which is BC-PRQ-06001. A second earlier failure is BC-SKL-03002, where a two layer composite is not differentiated correctly by the chain rule, so the learner cannot say what du should look like in the first place.
adaptive.remediation_target: BC-MIS-06017 (substitution requires the inner derivative, not merely a composite) for the conceptual failure; procedural loss once u is chosen correctly points instead to BC-ERR-06019 (constant factor from the differential dropped).

skills.assessability_basis: no archetype requiring at most two skills names this skill; assessable only inside multi-skill parts
skills.description_formal: Given a composite integrand, choose u equal to the inner expression such that the remaining factor is a constant multiple of du, and state the choice explicitly.
skills.description_plain: Pick u as the inside expression whose derivative is a factor of the integrand.
skills.name: Select a substitution by identifying an inner function whose derivative appears

diagnostic_archetypes: BC-QA-06008 (substitution carried through to back-substitution or converted limits, where applying original limits to an expression still in u forfeits the answer point)
adaptive.mastered_if: After antidifferentiating in u, every occurrence of u is replaced by g of x so the final expression names only the original variable, and the arbitrary constant is carried through to that last line. Nothing in the answer still refers to u, and the result can be differentiated back to the original integrand in the original variable. BC-ERR-06021 does not occur, meaning the arbitrary constant is present.
adaptive.partially_mastered_if: The antidifferentiation in u is correct and the answer is handed in still written in u, or the constant is dropped at the final line, BC-ERR-06021. The related failure BC-ERR-06018, original limits of integration kept after a substitution, shows the same underlying habit when the problem is definite, and that one removes eligibility for the answer point even where the number happens to be right.
adaptive.prerequisite_gap_if: The expression being back-substituted is already off by a constant multiple because the differential was never balanced, which places the failure at BC-SKL-06048. The tell is a clean and complete replacement of u by g of x on an antiderivative that was wrong before the replacement began.
adaptive.remediation_target: BC-ERR-06018 (the substituted variable is a different variable, so x limits and x answers cannot sit on a u expression) for the conceptual failure; a dropped constant with the back-substitution otherwise complete points to BC-ERR-06021 (constant of integration omitted).

skills.assessability_basis: no archetype requiring at most two skills names this skill; assessable only inside multi-skill parts
skills.description_formal: After antidifferentiating in u, replace u by g(x) so that the indefinite integral is expressed in the original variable, plus a constant.
skills.description_plain: Replace u by the original expression at the end.
skills.name: Back-substitute to express an indefinite integral in the original variable

common_confusions: BC-MIS-06016 (substitution renames a variable without changing the problem, so limits and differentials carry over unchanged)
diagnostic_archetypes: BC-QA-06008 (antiderivative or definite integral by substitution, where the integrand is a composite times a constant multiple of the inner derivative)
adaptive.mastered_if: The work commits to one bookkeeping route and stays there. Either the limits are rewritten as u values at the moment du is formed, or the antiderivative is carried back to x before the original endpoints are substituted, and the written line shows which route was taken. No line applies an x endpoint to an expression still carrying u, so BC-ERR-06018 (original limits kept after a substitution) is absent, and the endpoint evaluation on the definite integral from a to b reads consistently in a single variable.
adaptive.partially_mastered_if: The substitution itself is sound and the antiderivative in u is right, yet the final evaluation mixes variables, which is BC-ERR-06018 (original limits kept after a substitution) and blocks the answer point even when the arithmetic lands on the correct number (sg-23:17, sg-23:16). A second intermediate state shows the substituted endpoint expression written correctly but the numerical evaluation left undone, which under BC-FRQ-2026-Q5-A still earns the antiderivative point P1 and the value point P2 when the endpoint form is present (sg-26:18). An unsupported correct value with no antiderivative shown sits in the same band, earning P2 alone.
adaptive.prerequisite_gap_if: When the u expression is never returned to x at all, the failure belongs to BC-SKL-06049 (back-substitute to express an indefinite integral in the original variable) rather than to limit handling. When the endpoints are rewritten but with the wrong u values, the gap is BC-SKL-06050 (change the limits of integration when substituting in a definite integral), and the tell is a numerically clean evaluation of an antiderivative in u against endpoints that were never recomputed from the inner expression.
adaptive.remediation_target: Conceptual failure points to BC-MIS-06016 (substitution as a change of variable, not a relabelling), since the learner who believes u is shorthand has no reason to touch the limits at all. Procedural failure, where the change of variable is understood but the two routes are crossed mid-solution, points instead to BC-SKL-06050 (changing the limits of integration when substituting).

skills.assessability_basis: no archetype requiring at most two skills names this skill; assessable only inside multi-skill parts
skills.description_formal: Given a definite integral evaluated by substitution, either convert the limits to u values or back-substitute to the original variable before applying the original limits, and do not mix the two.
skills.description_plain: Keep the original limits only if you convert back to x first.
skills.name: Evaluate a definite integral by substitution with back-substitution before the limits are used

diagnostic_archetypes: BC-QA-06008 (antiderivative or definite integral by substitution, where the integrand is a composite times a constant multiple of the inner derivative)
adaptive.mastered_if: Recognition comes first. The integrand is read as a constant multiple of the derivative of an expression over that same expression, u is set to the denominator, du matches the numerator up to a constant, and the result is written as a constant times the natural logarithm of the absolute value of that expression plus C. The absolute value is present rather than dropped, which is what the logarithmic antiderivative point under BC-FRQ-2023-Q5-A rewards in either accepted form, and a definite version converts its limits rather than carrying x endpoints into u.
adaptive.partially_mastered_if: The pattern is spotted and u chosen well, but the constant adjustment on du is wrong, so the coefficient in front of the logarithm is off. Another partial state produces the logarithm without the absolute value or without the constant of integration, which BC-FRQ-2015-Q5-D records as an antidifferentiation notation loss after a correct decomposition (samples-15-q5:8). A third shows a reciprocal linear expression antidifferentiated incorrectly once the earlier closed form was right, the pattern BC-FRQ-2014-Q6-C describes when the derivative is found but its antiderivative is not. Under BC-QA-06008 a definite version that applies the original limits to an expression still in u is not eligible for the answer point (sg-23:17, sg-23:16).
adaptive.prerequisite_gap_if: An antiderivative written as a power of the denominator rather than a logarithm means the inner function was never identified as the object whose derivative sits in the numerator, which is BC-SKL-06047 (select a substitution by identifying an inner function whose derivative appears). Absolute value bars missing, or a logarithm of a product split wrongly across terms, points to BC-PRQ-06003 (logarithm rules and properties of the natural logarithm) rather than to substitution, and a du that never absorbs its constant points to BC-SKL-06048 (convert the differential and adjust the constant when substituting).
adaptive.remediation_target: BC-PRQ-06003 (the natural logarithm, its domain, and the absolute value inside the logarithm of a linear expression) is the conceptual target when the logarithmic form itself is not trusted. Procedural failure, where the form is known but the coefficient or differential is mishandled, points instead to BC-SKL-06048 (converting the differential and adjusting the constant).

skills.assessability_basis: no archetype requiring at most two skills names this skill; assessable only inside multi-skill parts
skills.description_formal: Given an integrand that is a constant multiple of the derivative of an expression divided by that expression, apply substitution to obtain a constant times the natural logarithm of the absolute value of that expression.
skills.description_plain: Recognise the derivative over the function pattern.
skills.name: Apply substitution to an integrand that antidifferentiates to a logarithm

diagnostic_archetypes: BC-QA-06016 (several integrands of different structure presented for classification and technique selection)
adaptive.mastered_if: Before any antidifferentiation, the degrees are compared and the improper rational integrand is divided, leaving a polynomial plus a remainder term whose numerator degree is strictly below the denominator degree. The quotient and remainder are written out as a sum, each piece is then matched to a basic antiderivative, and the division step appears on the page rather than being asserted. BC-ERR-06026 (improper rational integrand decomposed without a preliminary division) is absent, since nothing is split into partial fractions while the numerator still outranks the denominator.
adaptive.partially_mastered_if: A frequent intermediate state is the structural check skipped entirely, with partial fractions attempted straight away on an improper integrand, which is BC-ERR-06026 and leaves a decomposition that cannot be solved consistently, costing the antiderivative point. Elsewhere the division is started but the remainder is mishandled, so the proper term carries the wrong numerator while the polynomial part is correct. Under BC-QA-06016 the scoring of whichever technique is applied governs the outcome, since the CED frames this as selecting a procedure rather than as its own question type (ced:131).
adaptive.prerequisite_gap_if: If the long division itself breaks down, with terms misaligned or a remainder of the wrong degree, the failure is BC-PRQ-06009 (polynomial long division) and not integration. The tell is a learner who correctly announces that division is needed and then produces a quotient that does not reconstruct the original integrand when multiplied back through.
adaptive.remediation_target: BC-ERR-06026 (decomposing an improper rational integrand before dividing) marks the conceptual target, namely that a proper remainder is a precondition for the later technique. The procedural target when the precondition is recognised but the arithmetic fails is BC-PRQ-06009 (polynomial long division).

skills.assessability_basis: no archetype requiring at most two skills names this skill; assessable only inside multi-skill parts
skills.description_formal: Given a rational integrand whose numerator degree is at least the denominator degree, perform polynomial long division to write it as a polynomial plus a proper rational remainder before antidifferentiating.
skills.description_plain: Divide first so the remainder term is proper.
skills.name: Rewrite an improper rational integrand by polynomial long division

diagnostic_archetypes: BC-QA-06016 (several integrands of different structure presented for classification and technique selection)
adaptive.mastered_if: An irreducible quadratic denominator is rewritten as a perfect square plus a constant, the linear shift is absorbed by a substitution, and the resulting integral is named as the standard inverse trigonometric or logarithmic form it now matches. The constant pulled out during completion of the square is tracked rather than dropped, and the final answer is returned to the original variable. Where an inverse tangent form results, the constant outside and the constant inside the argument are both correct.
adaptive.partially_mastered_if: The square is completed correctly but the standard form is not recognised afterwards, so the work stalls at a rewritten denominator with no antiderivative attached. A second state completes the square with a sign or constant error, producing a form that looks standard but carries the wrong scaling factor. A third substitutes for the shifted variable and then never converts back. BC-QA-06016 places all of these under the scoring of the technique eventually applied, since the CED treats this topic as procedure selection (ced:131).
adaptive.prerequisite_gap_if: A quadratic that comes out of the completion step not equal to the original is BC-PRQ-06010 (completing the square), visible when expanding the learner's square does not reproduce the given denominator. If the completed form is correct but is not matched to an inverse trigonometric antiderivative, the gap is BC-SKL-06043 (antidifferentiate integrands whose antiderivatives are inverse trigonometric), and a shift that is never absorbed by a change of variable points to BC-SKL-06047 (select a substitution by identifying an inner function whose derivative appears).
adaptive.remediation_target: BC-SKL-06043 (recognising inverse trigonometric antiderivatives) is the conceptual target, because completing the square is pointless to a learner who does not know what form is being exposed. Procedural failure inside the algebra points instead to BC-PRQ-06010 (completing the square).

skills.assessability_basis: no archetype requiring at most two skills names this skill; assessable only inside multi-skill parts
skills.description_formal: Given an integrand with an irreducible quadratic denominator, complete the square and substitute so that the integral matches a standard inverse trigonometric or logarithmic antiderivative form.
skills.description_plain: Rewrite the quadratic as a square plus a constant to expose an inverse trigonometric or logarithmic form.
skills.name: Complete the square in a quadratic denominator to reach a standard form

diagnostic_archetypes: BC-QA-06016 (several integrands of different structure presented for classification and technique selection)
adaptive.mastered_if: A single fraction with a sum in the numerator is split term by term over its denominator, or a product of polynomials is multiplied out, and every resulting term is written as a power with an explicit exponent, including negative and fractional ones, before any antiderivative is taken. Constants are factored out cleanly, the reverse power rule is applied to each term separately, and a constant of integration accompanies the indefinite result. Radicals and reciprocals appear as powers rather than being carried in their original notation.
adaptive.partially_mastered_if: The rewrite is performed but one term keeps its original form, so the power rule is applied to some pieces and guessed at for others. A related state splits the numerator correctly and then mishandles a negative or fractional exponent when antidifferentiating. BC-FRQ-2021-Q3-C records a neighbouring pattern where a leading factor is taken as the stated volume, meaning the constant and the target value were confused rather than the method. Under BC-QA-06016, whichever technique ends up applied carries its own scoring behaviour (ced:131).
adaptive.prerequisite_gap_if: Terms that are antidifferentiated without ever being rewritten point to BC-PRQ-06001 (rewriting expressions to expose an inner function and its derivative), and the sign is a learner who accepts a compound integrand as it stands. Exponent arithmetic that fails on radicals or reciprocals belongs to BC-PRQ-06002 (exponent rules including negative and fractional exponents), while a correct rewrite followed by a wrong power antiderivative is BC-SKL-06040 (antidifferentiate power functions including negative and fractional exponents).
adaptive.remediation_target: BC-PRQ-06001 (rewriting to expose a form a basic rule can handle) is the conceptual target when the learner does not see rewriting as part of the method. When the rewrite happens but the exponents misbehave, the procedural target is BC-PRQ-06002 (exponent rules including negative and fractional exponents).

skills.assessability_basis: no archetype requiring at most two skills names this skill; assessable only inside multi-skill parts
skills.description_formal: Given an integrand that is a sum over a single denominator or a product of polynomials, rewrite it as a sum of terms each of which antidifferentiates by a basic rule.
skills.description_plain: Break a single fraction into separate terms or multiply out a product first.
skills.name: Rewrite an integrand by splitting or expanding before antidifferentiating

common_confusions: BC-MIS-06022 (technique choice follows the surface look of the integrand rather than its structural precondition)
diagnostic_archetypes: BC-QA-06016 (several integrands of different structure presented for classification and technique selection)
adaptive.mastered_if: The decision is justified from structure, not resemblance. Numerator and denominator degrees are compared first, the denominator is inspected for a factor whose derivative appears in the numerator, and only then is long division, completing the square, or substitution named, with the precondition for the chosen technique stated aloud. Techniques whose preconditions fail are ruled out explicitly, and where the first technique leaves a non basic integral a second is chained onto it. BC-ERR-06026 (improper rational integrand decomposed without a preliminary division) does not occur, because the degree check precedes everything.
adaptive.partially_mastered_if: One technique is selected correctly and executed, but the alternatives are never ruled out, so the choice reads as a guess that happened to land. Another intermediate state skips the structural check and decomposes an improper integrand directly, which is BC-ERR-06026 and yields a decomposition that cannot be solved consistently, losing the antiderivative point. A third names the right technique and then cannot state the condition it requires. BC-QA-06016 notes that the scoring behaviour of whichever technique is applied governs the result, since the CED frames the topic as procedure selection (ced:131).
adaptive.prerequisite_gap_if: If the technique is chosen correctly but the division that follows collapses, the gap is BC-SKL-06053 (rewrite an improper rational integrand by polynomial long division) or BC-PRQ-06009 (polynomial long division) rather than the decision itself. A correct call for an inverse trigonometric form followed by a broken rewrite points to BC-SKL-06054 (complete the square in a quadratic denominator) or BC-PRQ-06010 (completing the square), and a correct call for substitution with a badly chosen u points to BC-SKL-06047 (select a substitution by identifying an inner function whose derivative appears).
adaptive.remediation_target: BC-MIS-06022 (choosing a technique from resemblance to a worked example instead of from its precondition) is the conceptual target. Procedural failure, where the right technique is named and the execution then fails, points instead to BC-SKL-06053 (rewriting an improper rational integrand by long division) or BC-SKL-06054 (completing the square in a quadratic denominator), whichever technique was called.

skills.assessability_basis: no archetype requiring at most two skills names this skill; assessable only inside multi-skill parts
skills.description_formal: Given a rational integrand, compare the degrees of numerator and denominator and inspect the denominator for a factor whose derivative appears, and on that basis choose long division, completing the square, or substitution.
skills.description_plain: Check the degrees and the denominator structure before choosing.
skills.name: Decide between rearrangement and substitution for a rational integrand

common_confusions: BC-MIS-06019 (antidifferentiation treated as distributing across a product, so each factor is antidifferentiated on its own)
diagnostic_archetypes: BC-QA-06009 (antiderivative by integration by parts on a product of unlike factors, one of which simplifies on differentiation)
adaptive.mastered_if: All four of u, dv, du, and v are written down before the formula is invoked, and the assignment is defensible, with du simpler than u and v reachable by a basic antiderivative. A linear factor goes to the differentiated side and a trigonometric or exponential factor to the integrated side, matching the model solution in BC-FRQ-2024-Q5-D where the linear expression is differentiated and the cosine integrated with its chain factor carried (sg-24:18). BC-ERR-06022 (factors of a product antidifferentiated separately) is absent, so no answer is formed by multiplying two independent antiderivatives together.
adaptive.partially_mastered_if: The factors are assigned but exchanged, so the remaining integral grows in degree rather than shrinking, the pattern BC-FRQ-2024-Q5-D and BC-FRQ-2023-Q5-C both record when the choice rule is not applied. A separate state antidifferentiates each factor on its own and multiplies, which is BC-ERR-06022 and earns neither the u and dv point nor the expression point (sg-23:18, sg-24:18). Under BC-QA-06009 the choice may be left implicit and still credited, provided the correct parts expression or a tabular layout makes it visible (sg-23:18).
adaptive.prerequisite_gap_if: A sound assignment whose v then comes out wrong is a gap in the underlying antiderivative rather than in the choice, pointing to BC-SKL-06040 (antidifferentiate power functions including negative and fractional exponents) for a power factor or BC-SKL-06042 (antidifferentiate basic trigonometric integrands) for a sine or cosine factor. The tell is a learner who explains the choice rule correctly and then cannot produce v.
adaptive.remediation_target: BC-MIS-06019 (the sum rule wrongly extended to products) is the conceptual target, answerable by differentiating the proposed product and comparing it with the integrand. Procedural failure, where parts is correctly selected but v cannot be produced, points instead to BC-SKL-06042 (antidifferentiating basic trigonometric integrands).

skills.description_formal: Given a product integrand, select u and dv so that du is simpler than u and v is obtainable by a basic antiderivative, and record both u, dv, du, and v.
skills.description_plain: Assign one factor to differentiate and the other to antidifferentiate.
skills.name: Choose u and dv for an integration by parts

diagnostic_archetypes: BC-QA-06009 (antiderivative by integration by parts on a product of unlike factors, one of which simplifies on differentiation)
adaptive.mastered_if: When the integral left behind is still a product, parts is applied to it a second time and the alternating signs are tracked across both applications, so the sign attached to the third term is correct rather than copied from the second. Equivalently the work is laid out in a tabular arrangement whose sign column alternates and whose rows pair a derivative against an antiderivative. BC-ERR-06023 (minus sign dropped in the integration by parts expression) does not appear at either application, and the final collected expression reduces to a closed answer rather than an unfinished chain.
adaptive.partially_mastered_if: The second application is set up correctly but the sign from the first is not propagated through it, so one term carries the wrong sign, the situation BC-ERR-06023 describes when the response writes u times v plus the integral of v du, costing the expression point and the answer point that rests on it (sg-23:18). A different state performs the second application and then stops before collecting the terms into a single antiderivative. A tabular layout with the sign column omitted sits in the same band, since BC-QA-06009 credits the tabular arrangement only when the parts expression it encodes is recoverable.
adaptive.prerequisite_gap_if: If the first application is already malformed, the repetition inherits the fault and the gap is BC-SKL-06058 (apply the integration by parts formula), recognisable when the second pass is executed cleanly on an expression that was wrong before it started.
adaptive.remediation_target: BC-SKL-06058 (the parts expression itself) is the conceptual target when the repeated application reveals that the single application was never secure. Where the single application is sound and only the alternating signs across passes go wrong, the procedural target is BC-ERR-06023 (the minus sign in the parts expression).

skills.assessability_basis: no archetype requiring at most two skills names this skill; assessable only inside multi-skill parts
skills.description_formal: Given an integrand requiring repeated parts, apply the formula again to the remaining integral, keeping the signs consistent, or organise the work in a tabular arrangement.
skills.description_plain: Repeat the process when the new integral is still a product.
skills.name: Apply integration by parts more than once

diagnostic_archetypes: BC-QA-06009 (antiderivative by integration by parts on a product of unlike factors, one of which simplifies on differentiation)
adaptive.mastered_if: The boundary term u times v is evaluated at the upper limit and the lower limit and the difference taken, and the definite integral of v du over the same interval is subtracted from it, with the limits attached to both pieces rather than to one. The endpoint evaluation is shown, so the response does not rest on an unsupported value, and the answer is a number rather than an expression still carrying a constant of integration. BC-FRQ-2023-Q5-C notes that the parts expression may earn its points with the choice of u and dv left implicit and with limits present, absent, or partly present in that intermediate work (sg-23:18).
adaptive.partially_mastered_if: The boundary term is omitted altogether and only the remaining integral is evaluated, which BC-FRQ-2023-Q5-C records as the definite form of the parts expression not being used. Another state carries a constant of integration into a definite evaluation, and a third ignores a supplied integral value and tries to integrate an unspecified function symbolically, which BC-FRQ-2023-Q5-C lists as the given data not being used. Under BC-QA-06009 the three points sit on the choice of u and dv, the u times v minus the integral of v du expression, and the answer.
adaptive.prerequisite_gap_if: If the parts structure itself is wrong before any limits are applied, the failure belongs to BC-SKL-06058 (apply the integration by parts formula). If the structure is right and the endpoint arithmetic fails, with the upper and lower values subtracted in the wrong order or one endpoint never substituted, the gap is BC-SKL-06034 (evaluate a definite integral by antidifferentiation and endpoint substitution).
adaptive.remediation_target: BC-SKL-06058 (the parts expression) is the conceptual target when the boundary term is treated as optional, since the definite form of the formula was never internalised. Procedural failure confined to the endpoints points instead to BC-SKL-06034 (evaluating a definite integral by antidifferentiation and endpoint substitution).

skills.description_formal: Given a definite integral requiring parts, evaluate u times v at the upper and lower limits and subtract the definite integral of v du over the same interval.
skills.description_plain: Evaluate the uv boundary term at both limits and subtract the remaining integral.
skills.name: Evaluate a definite integral using integration by parts

diagnostic_archetypes: BC-QA-06009 (integrand is a product of unlike factors, one of which simplifies on differentiation, and parts is applied to an indefinite or definite integral)
adaptive.mastered_if: The integrand x times f prime of x is met by declaring u = x and dv = f prime of x dx, so du = dx and v = f of x, and the work then shows x times f of x evaluated at both limits minus the integral of f of x dx over the same interval, with the supplied values of f and the supplied integral of f substituted into their matching places. The parts expression appears in full before any number is moved, the boundary term keeps its limits, and the final line is expressed entirely in the given data rather than in an invented formula for f. Holds in the BC-QA-06009 archetype whether the data arrive as a table of values (BC-REP-04) or as symbolic statements (BC-REP-01).
adaptive.partially_mastered_if: Parts is selected and the u times v minus the integral of v du skeleton is written, which is enough for the first two points under BC-FRQ-2023-Q5-C where the choice of u and dv may stay implicit, but one of three things then goes wrong. The factors are exchanged, so f prime becomes u and x becomes dv, and the remaining integral is harder than the original. Or the boundary term x times f of x is dropped and only the integral piece survives, meaning the definite form of the parts expression was never used. Or the supplied value of the integral of f is left sitting unused while the response tries to antidifferentiate f itself.
adaptive.prerequisite_gap_if: Work that cannot get started because f prime of x is read as a new unrelated function rather than as the derivative of the f whose values were supplied points at BC-PRQ-06005, reading function notation and evaluation. The tell is a response that asks for a formula, or that writes f of x in place of f prime of x when forming v, confusing the function with its value at a point. A separate tell, the u times v minus the integral of v du template itself written wrongly on any integrand at all, points at BC-SKL-06058.
adaptive.remediation_target: BC-PRQ-06005 (function notation, so that f prime of x is recognised as the derivative of the tabulated f) covers the conceptual failure, while a failure that is procedural, the parts template itself mishandled, points instead to BC-SKL-06058 (applying the integration by parts formula).

skills.description_formal: Given an integrand of the form x times f prime of x with selected values or integrals of f supplied, apply parts with u = x and dv = f prime of x dx to express the result in terms of the supplied values.
skills.description_plain: Use parts when the integrand is x times f'(x) and only values of f are supplied.
skills.name: Apply integration by parts to an integrand containing an unknown function and its derivative

diagnostic_archetypes: BC-QA-06010 (rational integrand whose denominator factors into distinct linear factors, decomposed and antidifferentiated into natural logarithms)
adaptive.mastered_if: Before any decomposition is written, the denominator is factored into distinct nonrepeating linear factors and the degree of the numerator is checked against the degree of the denominator, so an improper integrand is divided first rather than split directly. Factoring a quadratic such as one whose roots differ produces two separate linear factors, each of which will later carry its own unknown constant, and the factored form is written out rather than held in the head. BC-ERR-06026, an improper rational integrand decomposed without a preliminary division, is absent from the work in BC-REP-01 symbolic form.
adaptive.partially_mastered_if: The denominator factors correctly but the structural check on the degrees never happens, which is BC-ERR-06026, so the decomposition that follows cannot be solved consistently and the antiderivative point is lost. A second intermediate state is visible in BC-FRQ-2015-Q5-D, where the factors are antidifferentiated one by one without any decomposition being written, showing the technique was not selected even though the factoring itself was fine. Partial factoring, one linear factor found and the rest left as a quadratic, is a third state.
adaptive.prerequisite_gap_if: No prerequisite skills are listed for this record, so a failure here is a factoring failure in its own right rather than a masquerade. The sign that the trouble sits below the calculus is a denominator whose roots are found numerically or by graphing rather than by factoring, leaving no linear factors to attach constants to.
adaptive.remediation_target: BC-SKL-06062 itself for the conceptual failure, recognising that a rational integrand must be both proper and factored before a decomposition exists; the procedural failure, factoring arithmetic that goes astray, is the same skill exercised on the algebra rather than on the structural check.

skills.assessability_basis: no archetype requiring at most two skills names this skill; assessable only inside multi-skill parts
skills.description_formal: Given a rational integrand, factor the denominator into linear, nonrepeating factors so that a partial fraction decomposition is available.
skills.description_plain: Factor the quadratic or higher denominator before decomposing.
skills.name: Factor a denominator into distinct linear factors

diagnostic_archetypes: BC-QA-06010 (rational integrand whose denominator factors into distinct linear factors, decomposed and antidifferentiated into natural logarithms)
adaptive.mastered_if: With the denominator already factored, unknown constant numerators are attached to each distinct linear factor, denominators are cleared to give a polynomial identity, and the constants come out either by substituting the root of each factor in turn or by equating coefficients of like powers. The solved constants are checked back in at least one convenient value, and the written decomposition is the one that BC-FRQ-2019-Q5-B awards its first point for and that BC-FRQ-2015-Q5-D awards two points for. The identity is treated as holding for all x, not only at the substituted values.
adaptive.partially_mastered_if: The decomposition is set up with the right shape but the constants come out wrong, which BC-FRQ-2015-Q5-D records as coefficients solved incorrectly, algebra rather than technique. A different stopping point appears in BC-FRQ-2019-Q5-B, where the decomposition is correct and complete and then nothing is antidifferentiated, so the technique is known but execution halts. A third state is a response that clears denominators but never forms a solvable system, substituting arbitrary values instead of the roots.
adaptive.prerequisite_gap_if: Constants that cannot be solved because the identity was never cleared properly, or because a small linear system is set up and then mishandled, points at BC-PRQ-06011, solving for undetermined coefficients in a rational identity. The tell is algebra that stalls after multiplying through. If instead the decomposition has the wrong number of terms, or a quadratic denominator still sits under one of them, the gap is BC-SKL-06062 and the denominator was never fully factored.
adaptive.remediation_target: BC-SKL-06062 (the factored denominator that determines how many constants there are) for the conceptual failure; the procedural failure, clearing and solving the identity, points instead to BC-PRQ-06011 (undetermined coefficients in a rational identity).

skills.assessability_basis: no archetype requiring at most two skills names this skill; assessable only inside multi-skill parts
skills.description_formal: Given a proper rational function with distinct linear factors, write the decomposition with unknown constant numerators, clear denominators, and solve for the constants by substitution or by equating coefficients.
skills.description_plain: Clear denominators and solve for the numerators.
skills.name: Solve for the constants in a linear partial fraction decomposition

diagnostic_archetypes: BC-QA-06010 (rational integrand whose denominator factors into distinct linear factors, decomposed and antidifferentiated into natural logarithms)
adaptive.mastered_if: Each term of the decomposition becomes its constant numerator times the natural logarithm of the absolute value of the linear factor, divided by that factor's leading coefficient, so a denominator such as two x minus three carries a one half out front. Absolute value bars appear inside every logarithm and a constant of integration is attached when the integral is indefinite, the two notation losses that BC-FRQ-2015-Q5-D names alongside an otherwise correct decomposition. The result is a sum of logarithm terms rather than a single logarithm, unless the terms are deliberately combined by the quotient rule.
adaptive.partially_mastered_if: The logarithm shape is right but the leading coefficient of the linear factor is not divided out, so the antiderivative is off by a constant multiple. Or, as BC-FRQ-2015-Q5-D records, the decomposition is right and the logarithms arrive without absolute values or without the constant, an antidifferentiation notation loss rather than a technique loss. A further state is the response in BC-FRQ-2019-Q5-B that attempts a substitution on the whole rational integrand instead, showing the integrand structure was not read as a sum of simple fractions.
adaptive.prerequisite_gap_if: Missing absolute value bars, or a logarithm of a product split wrongly, points at BC-PRQ-06003, the logarithm rules and the domain of ln. The tell is ln of a negative quantity written without comment. Constants that were already wrong before antidifferentiation began points at BC-SKL-06063 instead, and an inability to see one over a linear factor as a logarithm at all points at BC-SKL-06052.
adaptive.remediation_target: BC-SKL-06052 (substitution on an integrand that antidifferentiates to a logarithm) is the conceptual target, since it supplies the reason the reciprocal of a linear factor becomes a logarithm with a reciprocal leading coefficient; the procedural failure, absolute values and constants, points instead to BC-PRQ-06003 (logarithm rules and the domain of ln).

skills.assessability_basis: no archetype requiring at most two skills names this skill; assessable only inside multi-skill parts
skills.description_formal: Given a decomposition into ratios with linear denominators, antidifferentiate each term as the constant numerator times the natural logarithm of the absolute value of the linear factor divided by its leading coefficient.
skills.description_plain: Each simple fraction becomes a constant times a natural logarithm.
skills.name: Antidifferentiate a linear partial fraction decomposition

diagnostic_archetypes: BC-QA-06010 (rational integrand whose denominator factors into distinct linear factors, decomposed and antidifferentiated into natural logarithms)
adaptive.mastered_if: A proper rational integrand with distinct linear factors is decomposed, each term antidifferentiated as a constant times ln of the absolute value of its factor, and the Fundamental Theorem of Calculus applied by substituting the upper limit minus the lower limit. Logarithms are combined by the quotient rule where that simplifies the arithmetic, and the difference of logarithms is evaluated without dropping a sign or a coefficient. The final number is stated exactly, and the substitution of both limits is visible in the work rather than performed silently.
adaptive.partially_mastered_if: The decomposition and the antiderivative are both correct and then the endpoint arithmetic collapses, which BC-FRQ-2019-Q5-B describes as logarithm arithmetic wrong at the limits, algebra rather than the integration technique failing. A second intermediate state is the general antiderivative produced with no limits substituted at all, leaving the answer as an expression in x. A third is combining ln terms into a single logarithm incorrectly before substituting, so the quotient rule error is carried into the evaluation.
adaptive.prerequisite_gap_if: An antiderivative that is right but never evaluated at the endpoints, or evaluated as lower minus upper, points at BC-SKL-06034, evaluating a definite integral by antidifferentiation and endpoint substitution. The tell is the absence of the bracket evaluation line. If the logarithm terms themselves are misformed before any limit appears, the gap sits at BC-SKL-06064, and if the logarithm algebra at the limits is the problem, BC-PRQ-06003 is the place it originates.
adaptive.remediation_target: BC-SKL-06064 (antidifferentiating the decomposition into logarithms) for the conceptual failure; where the decomposition and antiderivative are sound and only the endpoint work fails, the procedural target is BC-SKL-06034 (definite integral by antidifferentiation and endpoint substitution).

skills.assessability_basis: no archetype requiring at most two skills names this skill; assessable only inside multi-skill parts
skills.description_formal: Given a definite integral of a proper rational function with distinct linear factors, decompose, antidifferentiate, and apply the Fundamental Theorem of Calculus, combining the logarithms where useful.
skills.description_plain: Decompose, antidifferentiate, then substitute the limits.
skills.name: Evaluate a definite integral of a rational function by partial fractions

diagnostic_archetypes: BC-QA-06011 (integral with an infinite limit of integration or an unbounded integrand, rewritten as a limit of definite integrals and evaluated or shown to diverge)
adaptive.mastered_if: Before any antidifferentiation, the integral is inspected at both limits and across the whole interval, and the response says in words which of the two causes applies, a limit of integration that is infinite or an integrand that is unbounded somewhere on the interval, including at an interior point rather than only at an endpoint. BC-FRQ-2019-Q5-C awards its first point for exactly this indication that the integral is improper. BC-ERR-06025, a finite value reported for a divergent integral, does not appear downstream because the impropriety was named before the evaluation began.
adaptive.partially_mastered_if: The infinite limit case is caught reliably and the unbounded integrand case is not, which BC-FRQ-2019-Q5-C records as the antiderivative evaluated at the endpoints directly with the singularity inside the interval never noticed. Another intermediate state names the integral improper without saying which cause, so the rewrite that follows has nowhere to put the variable. A third state calls a perfectly ordinary definite integral improper because the integrand is complicated rather than unbounded.
adaptive.prerequisite_gap_if: A response that recognises the infinite endpoint but cannot write it as anything other than a number points at BC-SKL-01054, writing an infinite limit using correct notation. The tell is infinity treated as an ordinary symbol in the limits of integration with no limit process available to describe it.
adaptive.remediation_target: BC-SKL-06066 itself for the conceptual failure, since the two causes of impropriety are the content of the skill; the procedural failure, writing the infinite endpoint down, points instead to BC-SKL-01054 (infinite limit notation).

skills.assessability_basis: no archetype requiring at most two skills names this skill; assessable only inside multi-skill parts
skills.description_formal: Given a definite integral, determine whether it is improper because one or both limits of integration are infinite or because the integrand is unbounded somewhere on the interval of integration, and name which.
skills.description_plain: Say whether the limit is infinite or the integrand is unbounded.
skills.name: Classify an integral as improper and name the cause

common_confusions: BC-MIS-06020 (infinity is a number that can be substituted)
BC-MIS-06021 (every improper integral of a decaying integrand converges)
diagnostic_archetypes: BC-QA-06011 (integral with an infinite limit of integration or an unbounded integrand, rewritten as a limit of definite integrals and evaluated or shown to diverge)
adaptive.mastered_if: Starting from the integral already written as a limit, an antiderivative of the correct form is found, both the variable endpoint and the fixed endpoint are substituted, and only then is the limit evaluated to a finite number, with the limit symbol retained on every line until the moment it is taken. Where the antiderivative is an exponential or a reciprocal power, its chain factor survives, the constant that BC-FRQ-2026-Q5-D notes gets dropped. The convergence is stated together with its value. BC-ERR-06024 and BC-ERR-06025 are both absent, so infinity is never substituted and no finite number is claimed for a limit that fails to exist.
adaptive.partially_mastered_if: The antiderivative is correct and the endpoint handling is not, as in BC-FRQ-2022-Q5-C where the antiderivative is evaluated at infinity directly and the loss is in the limit notation rather than the calculus, which is BC-ERR-06024. Or the limit is taken but the antiderivative carries a wrong leading constant because the chain factor was lost, which BC-FRQ-2023-Q5-B and BC-FRQ-2026-Q5-D both record while still allowing the antiderivative shape to be recognised. A third state produces a finite value where the limit is actually infinite, BC-ERR-06025.
adaptive.prerequisite_gap_if: Work that has no limit expression to evaluate because the improper integral was never rewritten points at BC-SKL-06067, and the tell is an antiderivative sitting directly against an infinite endpoint. If the limit machinery is fine and the bracket evaluation of the antiderivative at two endpoints is what fails, the gap is BC-SKL-06034 instead.
adaptive.remediation_target: BC-MIS-06021 (convergence inferred from a decaying integrand without examining the limit) is the conceptual target, with the integrals of one over x and one over x squared on the same infinite interval as the discriminating pair; the procedural failure, the antiderivative and its endpoint substitution, points instead to BC-SKL-06034 (antidifferentiation and endpoint substitution).

skills.description_formal: Given an improper integral written as a limit, find an antiderivative, evaluate at the variable and fixed limits, and evaluate the resulting limit to obtain the value of the convergent integral.
skills.description_plain: Antidifferentiate, substitute, then take the limit.
skills.name: Evaluate the limit to determine the value of a convergent improper integral

common_confusions: BC-MIS-06020 (infinity is a number that can be substituted)
BC-MIS-06021 (every improper integral of a decaying integrand converges)
diagnostic_archetypes: BC-QA-06011 (integral with an infinite limit of integration or an unbounded integrand, rewritten as a limit of definite integrals and evaluated or shown to diverge)
adaptive.mastered_if: When the limit of the definite integral is infinite or fails to exist, the response writes the word diverges, or states that the limit does not exist, as the answer, and offers no numerical value in its place. The limit is shown going to infinity first, so the conclusion rests on the evaluated limit rather than on the shape of the integrand. This is the conclusion step that BC-FRQ-2019-Q5-C withholds a point for when limits are written and no conclusion follows, and BC-ERR-06025, a finite value reported for a divergent integral, does not appear.
adaptive.partially_mastered_if: The limit is computed correctly and reaches infinity, then a finite number is written anyway on the answer line, which is BC-ERR-06025 and can come from an arithmetic slip inside the limit or from the assumption that every improper integral converges. A second state stops after the limit expression with no verbal conclusion at all, the missing communication step. A third treats divergence and convergence as interchangeable outcomes, reporting a value while also calling the integral divergent.
adaptive.prerequisite_gap_if: A response with nothing to conclude from, because no limit was ever set up, points at BC-SKL-06067 and the tell is an antiderivative evaluated straight at infinity, so the question of whether a limit exists was never posed.
adaptive.remediation_target: BC-MIS-06021 (an integrand approaching zero taken as sufficient for convergence) for the conceptual failure; where the divergence is understood and only the written conclusion is missing, the procedural target is BC-SKL-06069 itself as the statement step.

skills.assessability_basis: no archetype requiring at most two skills names this skill; assessable only inside multi-skill parts
skills.description_formal: Given an improper integral written as a limit, conclude that the integral diverges when the limit is infinite or does not exist, and state that conclusion rather than reporting a numerical value.
skills.description_plain: Say the integral diverges when the limit is infinite or fails to exist.
skills.name: Conclude that an improper integral diverges

diagnostic_archetypes: BC-QA-06011 (integral with an infinite limit of integration or an unbounded integrand, rewritten as a limit of definite integrals and evaluated or shown to diverge)
adaptive.mastered_if: An integral improper at both ends, or one whose integrand is unbounded at an interior point, is split at a convenient finite value so that each resulting piece carries exactly one source of impropriety, and the work states that the original converges only if every piece converges. For an interior singularity at c on the interval from a to b, the split is written as the integral from a to c plus the integral from c to b before any limit is taken, using the adjacent interval property. A single divergent piece is enough to end the question, and that is said rather than assumed.
adaptive.partially_mastered_if: The split happens at the right point but the two pieces are then handled as one limit with a single variable, so only one impropriety is addressed. Or the interior singularity is never found and the antiderivative is evaluated at the outer endpoints directly, which BC-FRQ-2019-Q5-C describes as the singularity inside the interval never being noticed. A third state splits correctly, finds one piece divergent, and still adds the two results together to report a number.
adaptive.prerequisite_gap_if: An interval that is not split at all, or split at a point that leaves an impropriety on both sides, points at BC-SKL-06066 when the cause of impropriety was never named. The tell is the absence of any statement about where the integrand is unbounded. If the split is attempted but the two integrals are not recombined correctly, or the sum property is applied with mismatched endpoints, the gap sits at BC-SKL-06031.
adaptive.remediation_target: BC-SKL-06066 (naming every cause of impropriety, interior ones included) for the conceptual failure; the procedural failure, the mechanics of breaking and rejoining the interval, points instead to BC-SKL-06031 (the adjacent interval property of definite integrals).

skills.assessability_basis: no archetype requiring at most two skills names this skill; assessable only inside multi-skill parts
skills.description_formal: Given an integral improper at both ends or at an interior point where the integrand is unbounded, split the interval at a convenient point so that each piece has one improper endpoint, and require every piece to converge.
skills.description_plain: Break the interval so each piece has a single source of impropriety.
skills.name: Split an improper integral that is improper at more than one place

common_confusions: BC-MIS-06017 (a composite integrand taken as a guarantee that substitution applies)
BC-MIS-06022 (technique chosen from visual resemblance to a worked example rather than the structural precondition)
diagnostic_archetypes: BC-QA-06016 (presents several integrands of different structure at once, so the classification is isolated from the execution of any one technique)
adaptive.mastered_if: Given a mixed set of integrands in BC-QA-06016, the response labels each one by the structural marker that decides the technique: a composite whose inner derivative is present up to a constant multiple goes to substitution with du written out, a product of unlike factors such as a polynomial times an exponential goes to parts, a rational form whose numerator degree is at least the denominator degree goes to long division first, a proper rational form with distinct linear factors goes to partial fractions, and an unbounded integrand or infinite limit is named improper before any antiderivative is written. Neither BC-ERR-06020 (substituting a composite when no constant multiple of the inner derivative appears) nor BC-ERR-06022 (antidifferentiating each factor of a product and multiplying) appears anywhere in the classification work.
adaptive.partially_mastered_if: Classification is right for the basic forms and for substitution but breaks on the rational and improper cases, or the correct technique is named while the precondition behind it is never stated. A common intermediate state is BC-ERR-06020, where a composite is routed to substitution on the strength of the inner function alone and the missing du is not noticed until the rewritten integral still contains the original variable. Another is BC-ERR-06022 on a product, where the two factors are antidifferentiated separately and multiplied instead of parts being named.
adaptive.prerequisite_gap_if: The integrand is never rearranged into a form where the marker is visible: constants are not factored out, a fraction is not split into terms, and a product is not rewritten so one factor is a constant multiple of the derivative of the other. That is an algebraic rewriting gap at BC-PRQ-06001, not a classification gap, and the tell is that the student classifies correctly once the rewritten integrand is handed to them. If instead the failure is confined to one branch, for example only the improper cases, the gap sits in the prerequisite skill for that branch, BC-SKL-06066.
adaptive.remediation_target: BC-MIS-06022 (the precondition, not the silhouette, selects the technique) for the conceptual case; the procedural case points instead to BC-PRQ-06001 (rewriting the integrand so the marker becomes visible)

skills.assessability_basis: no archetype requiring at most two skills names this skill; assessable only inside multi-skill parts
skills.description_formal: Given an integrand, classify it as a basic form, a composite with an available inner derivative, a product of unlike factors, an improper or factorable rational form, or an unbounded or infinite-limit integral, and name the corresponding technique.
skills.description_plain: Look at the structure and name the procedure it calls for.
skills.name: Classify an integrand to select an antidifferentiation technique

common_confusions: BC-MIS-06017 (presence of an inner function read as sufficient for substitution)
BC-MIS-06022 (surface resemblance to a worked example substituted for the structural test)
diagnostic_archetypes: BC-QA-06016 (the set includes integrands that look like substitution candidates but lack the inner derivative, so a rejection must be justified)
adaptive.mastered_if: The response states the structural condition the candidate technique requires and then points at the integrand to show the condition fails, for instance writing u for the inner expression, computing du, and showing that no constant multiple of du sits in the integrand, so substitution is ruled out rather than attempted. The elimination is stated as a condition and a witness, not as a report that the technique did not work out. BC-ERR-06020 is absent, since the technique is discarded before any substitution is carried through.
adaptive.partially_mastered_if: The technique is correctly rejected but the reason given is that the work became messy or did not simplify, with no named precondition. Alternatively the precondition is quoted correctly in general terms while the integrand itself is never referenced, so the rejection is not tied to the given expression. A weaker state still shows BC-ERR-06020, where substitution is written out in full and abandoned partway once the leftover variable will not cancel.
adaptive.prerequisite_gap_if: No technique is named at all, or the wrong family is named before the elimination is attempted, which places the failure one step earlier at BC-SKL-06071 (classifying the integrand). The tell is that the student can state a precondition accurately when told which technique is under consideration.
adaptive.remediation_target: BC-MIS-06017 (writing du and locating it in the integrand as the test substitution must pass) for the conceptual case; the procedural case points instead to BC-SKL-06071 (naming the candidate technique in the first place)

skills.assessability_basis: no archetype requiring at most two skills names this skill; assessable only inside multi-skill parts
skills.description_formal: Given an integrand and a candidate technique, state the structural condition the technique requires and explain why the integrand does or does not satisfy it.
skills.description_plain: Explain why a technique does not apply to a given integrand.
skills.name: Rule out a technique whose structural precondition is absent

diagnostic_archetypes: BC-QA-06016 (includes integrands where the first technique leaves a non basic integral, so chaining is required rather than optional)
adaptive.mastered_if: An integrand that no single technique resolves is carried through two stages: an opening rearrangement or substitution is performed, the resulting integral is re-inspected, and a second technique such as integration by parts or a partial fraction decomposition is applied to what remains, with the substitution variable returned to the original variable or the limits converted before the second stage begins. The chain is visible as two named steps with the intermediate integral written down, and the final antiderivative is consistent with the substitution actually made.
adaptive.partially_mastered_if: The first technique is executed correctly and the intermediate integral is written, but the work halts there because the remaining integral is treated as though it were already a basic form. Another intermediate state keeps the substitution variable into the second stage and reports an antiderivative in u while the question was posed in x, or applies parts to the rewritten integral without converting the limits of a definite integral after the substitution.
adaptive.prerequisite_gap_if: The second stage fails on its own mechanics rather than on the chaining, for example the u and dv assignment or the parts formula itself collapses, which is a BC-SKL-06058 gap, or the decomposition constants are wrong, which is a BC-SKL-06064 gap. If instead the first technique is chosen wrongly and the chain never had a chance, the failure belongs to BC-SKL-06071.
adaptive.remediation_target: BC-SKL-06071 (re-inspecting the integral produced by the first technique as a fresh classification problem) for the conceptual case; the procedural case points instead to BC-SKL-06058 (executing the parts formula on the remaining integral)

skills.assessability_basis: no archetype requiring at most two skills names this skill; assessable only inside multi-skill parts
skills.description_formal: Given an integrand that is not resolved by a single technique, apply an initial rearrangement or substitution and then a second technique such as parts or partial fractions to the resulting integral.
skills.description_plain: Apply one technique, then a second to what remains.
skills.name: Chain two antidifferentiation techniques in one problem

diagnostic_archetypes: BC-QA-06016 (mixes integrands that yield to a technique with ones that do not, so the response must decide when to stop)
adaptive.mastered_if: For an integrand with no closed-form antiderivative, such as an exponential of a squared argument or a sine of a reciprocal argument, the response stops looking for an elementary antiderivative and instead writes the required quantity as a definite integral with correct limits and integrand, then reports a numerical value from the calculator, carrying the calculator setup in the expression form BC-REP-09 rather than as a bare number. The integral expression itself stands as the answer when a value is not requested.
adaptive.partially_mastered_if: The integral is set up with the right integrand and limits but a fabricated elementary antiderivative is then written and evaluated, or the numerical value is reported with no integral expression shown, leaving the setup unearned. A further intermediate state gives the integral correctly and then loses the initial condition or the constant of the surrounding accumulation problem.
adaptive.prerequisite_gap_if: The integrand is not recognised as lacking an elementary antiderivative and technique after technique is attempted on it, which is a BC-SKL-06046 gap rather than a representation gap. The tell is that the student writes and evaluates the integral correctly once told no antiderivative exists.
adaptive.remediation_target: BC-SKL-06046 (which integrands have no elementary antiderivative) for the conceptual case; the procedural case points instead to BC-SKL-06071 (working through the technique preconditions before concluding none applies)

skills.assessability_basis: no archetype requiring at most two skills names this skill; assessable only inside multi-skill parts
skills.description_formal: Given an integrand with no closed-form antiderivative, represent the required quantity as a definite integral or approximate it numerically rather than attempting an elementary antiderivative.
skills.description_plain: Leave the answer as a definite integral or approximate it when no antiderivative is available.
skills.name: Recognise when no elementary technique applies and use an integral or numerical representation
